Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five

section: Romans 11:27 — The New Covenant to Israel: Client Nation Contract and the Fifth Cycle of Discipline
text: Romans 11:27 — The New Covenant to Israel: Client Nation Contract and the Fifth Cycle of Discipline

section: Romans 11:27 — The New Covenant to Israel: Client Nation Contract and the Fifth Cycle of Discipline
text: Romans 11:27 “and this will be my covenant with them when I take away their sins.” (ESV)

section: Romans 11:27 — The New Covenant to Israel: Client Nation Contract and the Fifth Cycle of Discipline
text: Corrected translation: Also, this is the covenant to them from me, when I have removed their punishment for sin.

section: Romans 11:27 — The New Covenant to Israel: Client Nation Contract and the Fifth Cycle of Discipline
text: Romans 11 has addressed the question whether God has cast away His people Israel. Having answered that question in the negative through a series of doctrinal principles, Paul now arrives at the heart of Israel's covenantal relationship with God. Verse 27 introduces the new covenant to Israel — the contractual basis upon which Israel will be restored as a client nation to God at the second advent of Christ. This chapter examines the exegesis of verse 27, the nature of the divine contracts, and the systematic classification of the covenants to Israel as a single five-paragraph contract.

section: I. Exegesis of Romans 11:27
text: I. Exegesis of Romans 11:27

section: The Conjunction kai and the Demonstrative Pronoun
text: The Conjunction kai and the Demonstrative Pronoun

section: The Conjunction kai and the Demonstrative Pronoun
text: The verse opens with the conjunction kai (καί), used here adverbially. In its conjunctive function it carries the force of also or therefore. The King James rendering 'for this' does not fully capture the adverbial nuance. The subject is the nominative feminine singular from the immediate demonstrative pronoun houtos (οὗτος), correctly rendered this, referring to Israel as a client nation. Paul employs ellipsis — a characteristic intensification device in New Testament Greek — omitting the verb. The verb to be must be supplied: also this is.

section: The Predicate Nominative: diatheke
text: The Predicate Nominative: diatheke

section: The Predicate Nominative: diatheke
text: The predicate nominative is diathēkē (διαθήκη), conventionally translated covenant but more precisely rendered contract. This is the new covenant to Israel, first given in Jeremiah 31:33–34. The term diathēkē refers not to a testamentary will — which requires the death of the testator — but to a binding contractual disposition made by one party in favor of another. God is Party of the First Part; Israel is Party of the Second Part.

section: The Indirect Object: autois
text: The Indirect Object: autois

section: The Indirect Object: autois
text: The indirect object is the dative from the intensive pronoun autos (αὐτός), used as a third person plural personal pronoun: to them. The indirect object specifies those in whose interest the new covenant was given — Israel, specifically the Jewish believers of the millennium who will have survived the tribulation and entered the millennial reign of Christ.

section: The Prepositional Phrase: apo plus ego
text: The Prepositional Phrase: apo plus ego

section: The Prepositional Phrase: apo plus ego
text: The prepositional phrase apo (ἀπό) plus the ablative of source from the first person pronoun egō (ἐγώ) is correctly translated from me, referring to God. The full clause to this point reads: Also, this is the covenant to them from me.

section: The Temporal Clause: hotan plus the Subjunctive
text: The Temporal Clause: hotan plus the Subjunctive

section: The Temporal Clause: hotan plus the Subjunctive
text: A temporal clause is introduced by the temporal conjunction hotan (ὅταν), which governs the subjunctive mood and introduces an indefinite temporal clause of contingency. The time referent is the second advent of Christ; the clause may be rendered when or whenever. With this is the aorist middle subjunctive of the verb aphaireo (ἀφαιρέω), meaning to remove, to take away something from someone. The aorist contemplates the second advent as a whole from the standpoint of its existing result. The middle voice is the indirect middle, emphasizing the Lord Jesus Christ as the agent fulfilling the new covenant to Israel. The subjunctive is a potential subjunctive implying future reference.

section: The Direct Object: hamartia and its Hebrew Background
text: The Direct Object: hamartia and its Hebrew Background

section: The Direct Object: hamartia and its Hebrew Background
text: The accusative plural direct object is hamartia (ἁμαρτία), conventionally translated sin. However, this is a quotation from the Hebrew of Jeremiah 31, and the underlying term is the Hebrew noun chata'th with its third masculine plural suffix. Chata'th means punishment for sin or punishment for idolatry — in this context, the fifth cycle of discipline administered to Israel in AD 70. The correct referent is not the removal of sins in some abstract sense but the removal of the historical, collective punishment — the fifth cycle of discipline — which has been in operation since AD 70 and which will be terminated at the second advent of Christ.

section: Corrected Translation of Romans 11:27
text: Corrected Translation of Romans 11:27

section: Corrected Translation of Romans 11:27
text: Also, this is the covenant to them — to the Jewish believers of the millennium — from me — from the Lord Jesus Christ as the God of Israel — when I have removed their punishment for sin, that is, when I have removed the fifth cycle of discipline.

section: Corrected Translation of Romans 11:27
text: The new covenant to Israel, then, emphasizes two things: the restoration of client nation Israel at the second advent of Christ, and the removal of Israel's historical collective punishment, the fifth cycle of discipline. Israel is not functioning as a client nation to God during the present church age, even though a Jewish state exists in the land. Client nation status cannot be restored until the second advent.

section: II. The New Covenant to Israel in Jeremiah 31
text: II. The New Covenant to Israel in Jeremiah 31

section: II. The New Covenant to Israel in Jeremiah 31
text: Romans 11:27 is a quotation from Jeremiah 31:33–34, and the interpretation of the verse requires examination of that passage in its original context.

section: II. The New Covenant to Israel in Jeremiah 31
text: Jeremiah 31:33–34 “But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they shall be my people. And no longer shall each one teach his neighbor and each his brother, saying, 'Know the LORD,' for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares the LORD. For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.” (ESV)

section: II. The New Covenant to Israel in Jeremiah 31
text: Corrected translation: But this is the contract which I will make with the house of Israel after those days — declares the Lord. After those days: after the elapsed church age, the termination of the tribulation, and the second advent of Christ. I will put my law within them and I will write it on their hearts. I will be their God and they shall be my people. They shall all know me from the least of them to the greatest — declares the Lord. Furthermore, I will forgive their iniquity and their sin I will remember no more.

section: II. The New Covenant to Israel in Jeremiah 31
text: The phrase 'after those days' specifies the elapsed interval of the church age, the tribulation, and the second advent. The failure of Israel under the old contractual administration was a failure of doctrine — not a failure of the contract itself. Israel memorized the Decalogue but used it as a basis for self-righteousness rather than understanding it as a definition of freedom under divine law. The new covenant addresses this failure by internalizing the law — writing it on the heart — as the condition of the restored millennial client nation.

section: II. The New Covenant to Israel in Jeremiah 31
text: The new covenant to Israel is also cited in Hebrews 8:8–13 and Hebrews 10:16–17. No passage, however, presents the contractual framework more lucidly in relation to Israel's eschatological future than Romans 11.

section: III. Definition and Classification of the Divine Contracts
text: III. Definition and Classification of the Divine Contracts

section: The Terms berith and diathēkē
text: The Terms berith and diathēkē

section: The Terms berith and diathēkē
text: The Hebrew term underlying the Old Testament covenants is berith (בְּרִית), and the Greek equivalent is diathēkē (διαθήκη). Both terms are conventionally translated testament in the titles 'Old Testament' and 'New Testament,' but this is a mistranslation. A testament is the will of a deceased person. Since God is eternal and cannot die, and since Christ in hypostatic union is resurrected and cannot die, the testamentary connotation is inapplicable. The correct rendering in both cases is covenant or contract. The designations 'Old Testament' and 'New Testament' should properly be rendered 'Old Covenant' or 'Old Contract' and 'New Covenant' or 'New Contract.'

section: The Definition of a Covenant
text: The Definition of a Covenant

section: The Definition of a Covenant
text: A covenant in the biblical sense is a contractual disposition made by Party of the First Part in favor of Party of the Second Part. The primary issue is divine favor — grace. Party of the First Part is always God: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit in their entirety, or an individual member of the Godhead in context. Party of the Second Part in the Old Testament covenants is always the nation Israel or the patriarchs who originated that nation. In the present church age, the Gentile client nation occupies a corresponding position as Party of the Second Part with respect to the operational principles derived from those contracts.

section: Eliminating the Conditional / Unconditional Classification
text: Eliminating the Conditional / Unconditional Classification

section: Eliminating the Conditional / Unconditional Classification
text: Traditional fundamentalist interpretation classifies the covenants as either conditional (the Mosaic Law) or unconditional (the Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, and new covenants). This classification is misleading and must be set aside. The Mosaic Law does contain conditional clauses because a client nation population is composed of believers and unbelievers, and failure to meet specified standards produces historical discipline. But the governing category is not conditionality — it is client nation status. The key to every covenant to Israel is the framework of the Jewish client nation, and that framework renders the conditional/unconditional distinction a secondary and often confusing consideration. There is neither reason nor theological purpose for any of the covenants to Israel apart from a client nation interpretation.

section: IV. The One Contract in Five Paragraphs
text: IV. The One Contract in Five Paragraphs

section: IV. The One Contract in Five Paragraphs
text: The five covenants to Israel are not five independent contracts. They constitute one master contract with five paragraphs, each paragraph addressing a specific dimension of client nation function. The contract as a whole defines how Israel is to operate under God's authority — in the past dispensation of Israel and in the future dispensation of the millennium.

section: Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant — Race
text: Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant — Race

section: Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant — Race
Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant — Race
text: The Abrahamic covenant defines the racial identity of the client nation. The nation Israel is constituted from those who carry the genetic line of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The covenant establishes divine law with respect to this race: the Jewish people are not to be persecuted as a race. Anti-Semitism is prohibited by this paragraph of the contract, and the historical record demonstrates that nations practicing anti-Semitism have invited destruction. A Jewish criminal is subject to the same jurisprudence as any other citizen; a Jewish citizen possesses the same civic standing as any other. The racial definition provides the people of the client nation; the subsequent paragraphs provide the land, the policy, the dynasty, and the future restoration.

section: Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant — Real Estate
text: Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant — Real Estate

section: Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant — Real Estate
text: The Palestinian covenant defines the territorial boundaries of client nation Israel — the real estate of the client nation. The land promised under this covenant belongs to the Jewish people by divine contract, not by the resolutions of international bodies or by claims of historical possession made by surrounding peoples. Arguments regarding so-called inalienable historical rights to the land that are advanced against the provisions of this covenant have no standing before the terms of the contract itself. The specific boundaries and provisions of the Palestinian covenant require detailed separate treatment, but the governing principle is unambiguous: the land is an assigned provision of God's contract with Israel.

section: Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Law — Policy
text: Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Law — Policy

section: Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Law — Policy
text: The Mosaic Law is the policy paragraph of the contract. It governs both believers and unbelievers within the client nation, addressing both spiritual and temporal dimensions of national life. The Mosaic Law divides into three codices.

section: Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Law — Policy
text: Codex One — the Decalogue — is fundamentally a definition of freedom, not merely a catalog of prohibited sins. Certain sins are prohibited because they constitute attacks upon freedom. The Decalogue also establishes the foundational authority structure: respect for God, respect for parents, respect for constituted authority. These are the operational prerequisites of a functioning free society.

section: Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Law — Policy
text: Codex Two — the Levitical ordinances — presents the gospel in the form of ritual with reality. The sacrificial system, the articles of tabernacle furniture, and the cycle of holy days (Passover, Day of Atonement, and others) together constitute a complete Christology and soteriology in typological form. Ritual without reality is dead religion; reality without understanding of the ritual misses the full pedagogical intent of this portion of the contract.

section: Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Law — Policy
text: Codex Three — the ordinances — provides the operational law for client nation government, addressing matters applicable to believer and unbeliever alike. It includes the laws of divine establishment: freedom through military victory, the principles of law enforcement, the standards of jurisprudence (innocence presumed until guilt is proven), the laws of commerce and free enterprise, the regulation of government authority, the tax structure (a straight ten-percent income levy applicable to all citizens regardless of economic status — a system that does not distort the incentives of free enterprise), the laws governing military function and service, criminal law, public health regulations concerning communicable disease, and the principles governing social order. The legislation on parental authority extended even to the provision that a demonstrably incorrigible minor, after due judicial process with the presumption of innocence, could be subject to capital punishment — a provision whose severity was designed precisely to prevent the social degeneracy that inevitably follows the breakdown of parental authority.

section: Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Law — Policy
text: The economic cycle embedded in Codex Three deserves particular attention. Free enterprise, operating under the laws of supply and demand without government interference, produces a seven-year economic cycle and a fifty-year complete cycle called the Year of Jubilee. The fiftieth year represents either the peak of prosperity before a cyclical correction or the point of greatest economic stress. Government interference with the free market disrupts this cycle and makes economic disaster inevitable. Similarly, the principle of universal military training — which teaches responsibility and the concepts of authority at the personal level — is an establishment requirement whose neglect produces both military vulnerability and social disorder.

section: Paragraph Four: The Davidic Covenant — Dynasty
text: Paragraph Four: The Davidic Covenant — Dynasty

section: Paragraph Four: The Davidic Covenant — Dynasty
text: Key texts: 2 Samuel 7:8–17; Psalm 89:20–37.

section: Paragraph Four: The Davidic Covenant — Dynasty
text: The Davidic covenant establishes the dynasty for the client nation — the question of who rules. The line of David is the dynastic line through which the ultimate ruler, the Lord Jesus Christ, will occupy the throne of Israel. This paragraph of the contract narrows the Messianic line from the tribe of Judah to the family of Jesse, father of David. The Davidic covenant thus integrates the Messianic promise with the governmental structure of the client nation: the ruler of the restored nation in the millennium will be the Lord Jesus Christ in hypostatic union, reigning from the throne of David.

section: Paragraph Five: The New Covenant to Israel — Restoration
text: Paragraph Five: The New Covenant to Israel — Restoration

section: Paragraph Five: The New Covenant to Israel — Restoration
text: The new covenant to Israel is the fifth and final paragraph of the contract. It is the restoration clause: the provisions by which client nation Israel will be renewed at the second advent of Christ and will function under His personal reign during the millennium. This is the paragraph quoted in Romans 11:27 and elaborated in Jeremiah 31:33–34, Hebrews 8:8–13, and Hebrews 10:16–17. All statements given in the new covenant must be interpreted in the context of the millennial reign of Christ, not in the context of the present church age.

section: Paragraph Five: The New Covenant to Israel — Restoration
text: The contract as a whole is perpetual. The five paragraphs are not currently operational because Israel has been under the fifth cycle of discipline since AD 70. During the present church age — the times of the Gentiles, the fullness of the Gentiles — only Gentile nations can function as client nations to God. The contract will resume its full operational force at the second advent. At that point the fifth cycle of discipline will be removed, Israel will be restored as a client nation, and the millennial modus operandi described in the new covenant will govern the restored nation.

section: V. The Covenants of the Messianic Line
text: V. The Covenants of the Messianic Line

section: V. The Covenants of the Messianic Line
text: Within the larger contractual framework, a sequence of covenants traces the Messianic line — the human genealogy through which the Lord Jesus Christ would enter the world. These covenants progressively narrow the line from the entire human race down to a single family.

section: V. The Covenants of the Messianic Line
text: The Adamic covenant (Genesis 2:15; 3:15) establishes the initial promise: the seed of the woman — the humanity of Christ — will come through the line of Adam. Man was created perfect and by his own free will sinned. The second Adam would enter the world perfect through the virgin birth and, by His own free will, would avoid personal sin, going to the cross to bear the sins of the world. Genesis 3:15 is the protoevangelium — the first announcement of the Messianic salvation program.

section: V. The Covenants of the Messianic Line
text: The Noahic covenant (Genesis 6:18; 8:21–9:17) reiterates the Messianic promise in the context of the narrowing of Adam's line. The line runs through Seth, son of Adam. At the generation of Noah, the three sons — Shem, Ham, and Japheth — represent distinct streams of the human race. The Messianic line continues through the Semitic line of Shem.

section: V. The Covenants of the Messianic Line
text: The Abrahamic covenant (Genesis 12:1–3; 13:15–16; 15:18; 22:15–18; 26:3–4; Exodus 6:2–8) narrows the Messianic line further. From the broad Semitic grouping — which includes Arabs, Syrians, Chaldeans, and numerous other peoples — the line is specified as running through Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. This means the Messianic line is the Jewish line.

section: V. The Covenants of the Messianic Line
text: The Davidic covenant (2 Samuel 7:8–17; Psalm 89:20–37) narrows the line still further. From the twelve sons of Jacob and the thirteen tribes of Israel, the line runs through the tribe of Judah, and within Judah through the family of Jesse, father of David. The Messianic humanity of Christ descends from David.

section: V. The Covenants of the Messianic Line
text: The new covenant to Israel completes the sequence: the seed of the woman will return to the earth a second time to restore Israel and to establish the conditions of perfect environment in the millennial reign. The millennial reign demonstrates both the grace of God in restoring a nation that had failed repeatedly under the contract, and the intractability of the sin nature — perfect environment in the millennium will not solve the human problem any more than perfect environment solved it in Eden. At the end of the thousand years, a final revolt (the Gog-Magog revolution of Revelation 20) will demonstrate conclusively that environmental improvement is never the solution to man's problem. Man's problem is in the soul. The only resolution is salvation — regeneration, the new birth.

section: V. The Covenants of the Messianic Line
text: The sequence of covenants in the Messianic line — Adamic, Noahic, Abrahamic, Davidic, and new covenant to Israel — forms a subsidiary structure within the larger five-paragraph contract to Israel. Together they establish both the identity of the Savior and the framework within which He will rule.

section: VI. The Church Age Contract and its Relation to Israel's Contract
text: VI. The Church Age Contract and its Relation to Israel's Contract

section: VI. The Church Age Contract and its Relation to Israel's Contract
text: In addition to the five-paragraph contract to Israel, God has made a separate contract applicable to the church age. This contract governs the royal family of God — church age believers — in their distinct dispensational role. The church age contract is grounded in the thirty-six things received at the moment of salvation and in the specific plan God has designed for the church age.

section: VI. The Church Age Contract and its Relation to Israel's Contract
text: While the two contracts are distinct, the Mosaic Law's third codex — the establishment ordinances — contains principles applicable to any client nation in any dispensation. The laws of free enterprise, the principles of jurisprudence, the standards of military function, the taxation framework, and the regulations of social order are not ceremonial or typological provisions. They are universal establishment principles. A Gentile client nation in the church age that disregards these principles is subject to the same sequence of historical discipline — the five cycles — that disciplined Israel.

section: VI. The Church Age Contract and its Relation to Israel's Contract
text: The study of Israel's covenants is therefore directly relevant to the church age client nation. Understanding what Israel had, why it lost client nation status, and what provisions govern its future restoration illuminates the contractual obligations and vulnerabilities of any nation that has functioned under divine client nation assignment.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five
text: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five
text: 1. Romans 11:27 is a covenantal citation, not a soteriological statement. The verse does not address the removal of personal sin in any general sense. It quotes Jeremiah 31 to affirm that the fifth cycle of discipline administered to Israel in AD 70 will be terminated at the second advent of Christ, and that the new covenant to Israel — the restoration clause of the five-paragraph contract — will then become fully operational.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five
text: 2. The word diathēkē means contract, not testament. A testament requires the death of the testator. Since God is eternal and Christ in hypostatic union is resurrected and cannot die, both 'Old Testament' and 'New Testament' are mistranslations. The correct designations are Old Covenant/Contract and New Covenant/Contract.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five
text: 3. The five covenants to Israel constitute a single contract in five paragraphs. Paragraph one (Abrahamic) defines the race of the client nation. Paragraph two (Palestinian) defines the real estate. Paragraph three (Mosaic Law) defines the policy, both spiritual and temporal. Paragraph four (Davidic) defines the dynasty. Paragraph five (new covenant to Israel) defines the restoration at the second advent and the millennial modus operandi.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five
text: 4. The conditional/unconditional classification of the covenants is misleading and must be set aside. The governing category is client nation status. Under that framework, the presence of conditional clauses in the Mosaic Law reflects the mixed believing and unbelieving composition of any national population, not a fundamental difference in the nature of the covenant itself.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five
text: 5. The Messianic line is traced through five covenants: Adamic, Noahic, Abrahamic, Davidic, and new covenant. Each covenant narrows the line: from all humanity, to the Semitic line, to Abraham's seed, to the tribe of Judah and the family of David. The new covenant completes the sequence by specifying the second advent as the moment of full Messianic fulfillment.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five
text: 6. The fifth cycle of discipline against Israel began in AD 70 and remains in operation throughout the church age. The times of the Gentiles is the period during which Gentile nations — not Israel — function as client nations to God. Israel's contract is not terminated but suspended. It will resume at the second advent when the fifth cycle is removed.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five
text: 7. The Mosaic Law's establishment codex contains principles applicable to any client nation in any dispensation. Free enterprise economics, the presumption of innocence in jurisprudence, universal military service and the cultivation of personal discipline and authority-orientation, a flat tax rate that does not suppress economic motivation, and the maintenance of parental authority — these are not ceremonial provisions but universal establishment laws. Their violation by any client nation, including in the present church age, produces predictable historical consequences according to the five cycles of discipline.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five
text: 8. Perfect environment does not resolve the problem of the sin nature. The millennium will demonstrate this finally and definitively. Just as Adam sinned in a perfect environment by the exercise of his free will, the Gog-Magog revolt at the close of the millennium will demonstrate that environmental improvement cannot produce salvation, happiness, or conformity to divine standards. The only resolution to man's problem is regeneration — faith in Jesus Christ as Savior.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Five
text: 9. The new covenant to Israel must be interpreted entirely within a millennial context. All of its provisions — internalized law, universal knowledge of the Lord, forgiveness of iniquity — describe the conditions that will obtain in the restored client nation under the personal reign of Christ. They do not describe conditions applicable to the present church age, nor are they fulfilled in any institutional or ecclesiastical sense prior to the second advent.

section: Romans 11:25–27 — The Covenants of the Contract: Abrahamic, Palestinian, and Mosaic Covenants — Client Nation Theology
text: Romans 11:25–27 — The Covenants of the Contract: Abrahamic, Palestinian, and Mosaic Covenants — Client Nation Theology

section: Romans 11:25–27 — The Covenants of the Contract: Abrahamic, Palestinian, and Mosaic Covenants — Client Nation Theology
text: Romans 11:25–27 “Lest you be wise in your own sight, I do not want you to be unaware of this mystery, brothers: a partial hardening has come upon Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in. And in this way all Israel will be saved, as it is written, 'The Deliverer will come from Zion, he will banish ungodliness from Jacob'; 'and this will be my covenant with them when I take away their sins.'” (ESV)

section: Romans 11:25–27 — The Covenants of the Contract: Abrahamic, Palestinian, and Mosaic Covenants — Client Nation Theology
text: Corrected translation: Brethren — royal family of God — I do not wish you to be ignorant of this mystery, that you stop being wise in your own estimation: that the hardening in part has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in. And so all Israel — the Jews of the Tribulation — shall be delivered, just as it stands written: He who delivers will come from Zion; He will remove godless ones from Jacob. And this is the covenant to them from Me, when I have removed their punishment for sin.

section: Romans 11:25–27 — The Covenants of the Contract: Abrahamic, Palestinian, and Mosaic Covenants — Client Nation Theology
text: Romans 11:25–27 introduces what Paul calls a mystery — Church Age doctrine not previously revealed — concerning Israel's partial hardening and the certainty of her future deliverance. The passage grounds that certainty in a covenant, here designated 'the contract' in its several paragraphs. Having established in prior chapters that Israel's hardening is neither total nor final, Paul now discloses the divine mechanism: a series of covenants made with Israel as client nation that guarantee her ultimate restoration. This chapter examines the theological content of that contract — the Abrahamic, Palestinian, and Mosaic covenants — and draws out the principles applicable to any client nation, including the Church Age Gentile client nation.

section: I. The Mystery and Its Purpose
text: I. The Mystery and Its Purpose

section: I. The Mystery and Its Purpose
text: Paul's designation of his disclosure as a 'mystery' (

section: I. The Mystery and Its Purpose
text: Paul's designation of his disclosure as a mystērion — μυστήριον — signals that the content belongs specifically to the previously unrevealed body of Church Age doctrine. The mystery is not that Israel would eventually be saved; the Old Testament prophets had declared that openly. The mystery is the precise mechanism: Israel's hardening is partial and temporary, calibrated to the ingathering of the Gentiles, and when that fullness is complete, the deliverer comes from Zion and the covenant is executed. Ignorance of this mystery, Paul warns, produces arrogance — the presumption that Gentile believers have permanently displaced Israel in the plan of God.

section: I. The Mystery and Its Purpose
text: The corrected translation renders the warning as 'stop being wise in your own estimation.' The present imperative with a negated ongoing action implies that the Roman believers were already cultivating this arrogance. Ignorance of the mystery is both the cause and the symptom: when Church Age doctrine is absent from the soul, arrogance fills the vacuum. The remedy is the intake of the revealed mystery — the full content of Paul's argument in Romans 9–11.

section: II. The Contract: Covenant Framework for Client Nation Israel
text: II. The Contract: Covenant Framework for Client Nation Israel

section: II. The Contract: Covenant Framework for Client Nation Israel
text: The covenant referenced in verse 27 — 'this is my covenant with them' — is not a single document but a series of interlocking paragraphs that together constitute the divine contract with Israel as client nation. Each paragraph addresses a specific dimension of client nation function: race and population vigor, geography and property, policy and freedom. Understanding these paragraphs is prerequisite to understanding both Israel's historical trajectory and the principles governing any subsequent client nation.

section: A. Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant
text: A. Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant

section: A. Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant
text: The Abrahamic covenant is the foundational grace paragraph of the contract. God as party of the first part made favorable disposition to Abraham as party of the second part — unconditionally, apart from any merit on Abraham's side. The covenant defines the Jewish race as the citizenry of the first and last client nation in biblical history. Its provisions are first stated in Genesis 12:1–3 and progressively elaborated through Genesis 13, 15, 17, and 22.

section: A. Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant
text: Several structural principles emerge from this paragraph.

section: A. Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant
text: First, the covenant establishes that client nation vigor is spiritual, not biological. The argument that some races are inherently superior to others is historically and theologically untenable. The Jews received their invigoration from a spiritual factor — the justice of God acting toward a people whose patriarchs had made the salvation adjustment and continued in maturity adjustment. Red, yellow, black, and white alike are eligible for the identical spiritual invigoration. The determining variable is never anthropological classification; it is always the soul.

section: A. Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant
text: Second, the covenant was confirmed in sequence. It was confirmed to Isaac — not to Ishmael or to the sons of Keturah — in Genesis 26:3–4. It was confirmed to Jacob — not to his twin Esau — in Genesis 35:12. That twins from the same womb receive different covenantal standing demonstrates conclusively that the differentiating factor is not genetic. The difference between Jacob and Esau was a spiritual factor, expressed through the exercise of volition toward doctrine.

section: A. Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant
text: Third, the covenant was the basis for the divine deliverance of the Jews from four hundred years of Egyptian slavery. Most people groups subjected to a single century of slavery disappear within three or four generations. The Jews endured four centuries and in one generation made the transition to freedom. The mechanism was the spiritual factor operative through the Abrahamic covenant promise.

section: A. Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant
text: Fourth, the mechanics of the Abrahamic covenant demanded spiritual maturity at its very inception. The entire future of the client nation hung at one point upon two people: a man of ninety-nine years and a woman of ninety who was past the physiological capacity for childbearing. From Abraham and Sarah, by divine intervention, came the vigorous new race. The mechanism was ultra-supergrace blessing — the maximum expression of maturity adjustment to the justice of God — applied to two individuals whose bodies could no longer support the promise apart from divine action.

section: A. Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant
text: Fifth, the covenant was confirmed through the ritual of circumcision (Genesis 17:9–14) as an external sign of an internal spiritual reality. Ritual without the corresponding doctrinal content is meaningless; the circumcision pointed to the cutting away of dependence upon the old sin nature and the establishment of a new race whose identity was spiritual before it was ethnic.

section: A. Paragraph One: The Abrahamic Covenant
text: Sixth, the ultimate scope of blessing declared in Genesis 22:15–18 encompasses both individual imputation of blessing to the mature believer and blessing by association — the mechanism by which a client nation becomes the conduit of divine blessing to all other nations in a given historical period. This is the foundational statement of client nation purpose.

section: B. Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant
text: B. Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant

section: B. Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant
text: The second paragraph of the contract is the Palestinian covenant, the real estate provision. Its central principle is straightforward: a client nation cannot function without a specific geographical location on planet earth. No client nation has ever existed in the abstract; each has occupied a defined territory. The sanctity of that territory — as property belonging to a people — is the material prerequisite for evangelism, spiritual growth, and missionary activity.

section: B. Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant
text: The land grant to Israel was first proclaimed in indefinite terms: Abraham was instructed to stand on high ground and look in all compass directions, with the assurance that everything visible would belong to his progeny (Genesis 13:14–15; 15:18). Specific boundaries were later given to Moses in Numbers 34:1–12. The boundaries include, on decipherment of the ancient national names: the Mediterranean Sea as the western border; the territory of the Hittite empire — corresponding approximately to modern Turkey — as the northwestern border; the Nile River as the southern border, taking in eastern Egypt and eastern Ethiopia; the Trans-Jordan region and Iraq to the east; and the Euphrates River as the northeastern boundary. The total territory encompasses the entire Middle East — a grant of a magnitude Israel has never militarily occupied.

section: B. Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant
text: This observation generates the hermeneutical key to the Palestinian covenant: in the past dispensation, Israel could only possess what its military establishment could conquer and hold. The peak of that possession came in the reign of Solomon. From Solomon onward, the trajectory was decline. The present modern state of Israel holds only what its current military capability can sustain. But the full extent of the land grant awaits the second advent and the millennial reign of the Lord Jesus Christ, when swords will be beaten into plowshares not by political will but by the personal intervention of the God of Israel. At that point, Israel will receive what she could never take by arms.

section: B. Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant
text: Both Jeremiah and Ezekiel confirm the millennial fulfillment. Jeremiah 32:36–44 and Ezekiel 11:16–21 and 36:21–38 describe the land restoration in eschatological terms that exceed any historical precedent. The millennial Red Sea will be dried up as part of the geographical reconfiguration that delivers the full land grant. This is an entirely future reality, never yet occupied, still awaiting execution.

section: B. Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant
text: Several principles of property theology emerge from this paragraph. First, no client nation can exist without the sanctity of private property. When the state owns all property, the people are slaves regardless of what political vocabulary surrounds that ownership. Freedom requires that individuals and legitimate collective organizations have the right to acquire, hold, use, and transmit property. The Palestinian covenant establishes this principle in the very structure of the divine land grant. Even within Israel's covenant tenure, sold property was to be returned to its original owner in the year of Jubilee every fiftieth year — a provision that expresses the divine commitment to distributed private ownership rather than concentration or confiscation.

section: B. Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant
text: Second, property cannot be maintained without a military establishment capable of defending it. In the ancient world the same institution both gained and guaranteed territory. In modern states those functions are distributed between military and law enforcement, but the underlying principle is identical: property rights without enforcement capacity are theoretical abstractions. Any nation that degrades its military forfeits the material basis of the freedom that makes client nation function possible.

section: B. Paragraph Two: The Palestinian Covenant
text: Third, ownership of property generates personal responsibility. The individual who has earned, purchased, and managed property has a stake in the social order that produces and protects such ownership. The erosion of property rights — through confiscatory taxation, nationalization, or enforced redistribution — correspondingly erodes the population's sense of civic responsibility and investment in ordered liberty. This is the mechanism by which client nations decline: the spiritual factor decays, the property ethic erodes with it, and the institutional structures of freedom collapse in sequence.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: The third major paragraph of the contract is the Mosaic covenant — the comprehensive policy code given to Israel as client nation. It was given specifically to Israel (Exodus 19:3; Leviticus 26:46; Romans 3:19; 9:4), not to any Gentile nation in its totality, and not to the Church (Acts 15:5, 24; Romans 6:14; Galatians 2:19). Its application to the Church Age is as pattern and principle, not as direct obligation.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: The Mosaic covenant divides into three codices, each addressing a distinct dimension of client nation life.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: Codex One is the Decalogue — the Ten Commandments. The theological purpose of the Decalogue is frequently misunderstood in Reformed and Calvinist traditions as a comprehensive definition of sin. In fact the Decalogue defines freedom: it identifies the conditions under which human beings can exercise genuine self-determination. The prohibitions against theft, murder, and adultery are protections of property, life, and the sanctity of the marital covenant respectively. The command to love God with all one's heart and soul identifies the motivational foundation without which establishment principles cannot function correctly. Sin is a far broader category than the negative imperatives of the Decalogue; the Decalogue's function is to establish the perimeter conditions for a free society.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: Codex Two is the spiritual code — the ordinances. This body of legislation authorized the Levitical priesthood, the tabernacle and later the temple, the holy days, and the sacrificial system. Its theological content is entirely Christological: the furniture of the tabernacle, the Levitical offerings, the priestly mediatorial function, and the calendar of holy days all communicate the person and work of the Lord Jesus Christ in type and shadow. The spiritual heritage of Israel — its complete Christology and soteriology — was perpetuated not by physical birth but through this ritual-doctrinal system, which required a new birth for its appropriation. The title 'Lord of Hosts' (God of the armies) applied throughout the Old Testament to the God of Israel identifies the Lord Jesus Christ as the divine warrior who is both the origin of establishment principles and the guarantor of the client nation's military existence.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: Codex Three is the establishment code — the judgments. This is the comprehensive policy manual for client nation modus operandi. It encompasses freedom and privacy; marriage law; military policy; legitimate taxation by fixed percentage; diet, health, sanitation, and quarantine regulations; laws of jurisprudence including standards of evidence, trial procedure, and punishment; free enterprise and the legitimacy of profit motivation. Several principles in Codex Three deserve emphasis.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: Military policy: universal military training appears in the book of Numbers — the title of which in Hebrew means 'enlistees' or 'draftees,' the census being a military muster. The book of Numbers is the divine textbook on how a client nation functions under organized military obligation. Universal military training serves the additional social function of imparting an understanding of authority to those who have not yet acquired it through property ownership or family responsibility.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: Taxation: the tithe — a fixed percentage — is the biblical model of legitimate taxation. A flat percentage applied uniformly is just; progressive confiscatory rates that penalize productivity are not. The principle that profit is legitimate and that penalizing profit is immoral is embedded in Codex Three.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: Separation of church and state: Codex Three explicitly separates the Levitical priesthood from the civil government, establishing the principle that spiritual institutions and political authority must operate in distinct spheres. The church building as a concept — property held collectively for spiritual purpose, exempt from civil taxation — is a legitimate perpetuation of this Mosaic principle into the Church Age.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: The Mosaic Law authorizes the Levitical sacrifices as communicative shadows pointing to the Lord Jesus Christ. The shadows were fulfilled at the cross (Matthew 5:17; Romans 10:4; Hebrews 9:12–13, 18–22; 10:1). Today the function of communicating the person and work of Christ is carried by the gift of evangelism and the ministry of personal and collective proclamation.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: A series of critical negative clarifications must be noted. Keeping the Mosaic Law was never the basis of salvation or spirituality (Romans 3:20; Galatians 2:16; Romans 3:28; Philippians 3:9). The law cannot give eternal life (Galatians 3:21). The law cannot provide the Holy Spirit (Galatians 3:2). The law cannot resolve the problem of the old sin nature (Romans 8:3). Patriotism is not salvation. The law's function was always the modus operandi of a client nation — the vehicle of freedom within which the spiritual heritage could be perpetuated — never the mechanism of justification before God.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: The Mosaic Law has been set aside in two senses. First, the Lord Jesus Christ fulfilled its types and shadows at the cross, removing the obligation of Levitical ritual for both Jew and Gentile believer in the Church Age. Observation of the Sabbath day, dietary restrictions, and the sacrificial calendar no longer apply as obligations. Second, it is set aside as a direct legislative code for Church Age believers and client nations. But its principles are never set aside: the cycles of discipline found in Codex Three still function; the principle of universal military training still applies to any client nation seeking to maintain freedom; fixed-percentage taxation is still the just model; the sanctity of property is still the foundation of ordered liberty.

section: C. Paragraph Three: The Mosaic Covenant
text: The current purpose of the Mosaic Law may be stated in four ways. First, it provides a pattern for Gentile client nation function in the areas of freedom, military establishment, taxation, government structure, and free enterprise. Second, it is written for the believer's instruction (Romans 15:4). Third, it is written as the believer's example (1 Corinthians 10:11–12). Fourth, it establishes the divine standard of reality that any client nation must engage if it is to continue in that status.

section: III. Client Nation Principles Derived from the Contract
text: III. Client Nation Principles Derived from the Contract

section: III. Client Nation Principles Derived from the Contract
text: The covenantal structure examined above generates a set of durable principles applicable to any national entity functioning as a client nation to God in history.

section: III. Client Nation Principles Derived from the Contract
text: The spiritual factor is always determinative. Race, geography, climate, genetics, and material resources are variables. The spiritual factor — the presence of a body of mature believers whose adjustment to the justice of God sustains divine blessing on the nation — is the constant. Israel's 400-year survival of Egyptian slavery, her emergence as a client nation from that slavery in a single generation, the supernatural birth of Isaac from Abraham and Sarah, the differential covenant standing of Jacob over Esau — all demonstrate that the spiritual factor overrides every natural variable.

section: III. Client Nation Principles Derived from the Contract
text: Freedom is the vehicle. Evangelism, spiritual growth, and missionary activity require freedom. Freedom requires property. Property requires military defense. Military capability requires population vigor. Population vigor requires the spiritual factor. The chain is not reversible: you cannot manufacture the spiritual factor through superior military organization, economic prosperity, or legal engineering. The spiritual factor must come first, and everything else is its by-product.

section: III. Client Nation Principles Derived from the Contract
text: The pivot of mature believers is the client nation's indispensable asset. Without a sufficient body of believers who have cracked the maturity barrier, there is no pivot. Without a pivot, the spiritual heritage cannot be perpetuated. Without perpetuation of the spiritual heritage, the freedom structures erode. Without freedom, client nation function ceases. Israel went down through this sequence under the five cycles of discipline. The sequence is not unique to Israel.

section: III. Client Nation Principles Derived from the Contract
text: The millennial resolution of the contract is certain. Whatever the present state of client nation Israel's dispossession — now under the fifth cycle of discipline, scattered among the nations since A.D. 70 — the contract is permanent. The land grant will be executed in full at the second advent. 'All Israel shall be delivered' is not conditional on Israel's performance; it is conditioned on the coming of the Deliverer from Zion. The reliability of the contract is the reliability of the God of Israel, who is the Lord Jesus Christ.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 1. The mystery of Romans 11:25–27 is specifically Church Age doctrine: Israel's hardening is partial and temporary, calibrated to the fullness of the Gentiles, and terminates at the second advent when the covenant is executed in full. Ignorance of this mystery generates arrogance — the presumption that Gentile believers or client nations have permanently displaced Israel in the plan of God.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 2. The covenant referenced in verse 27 is a multi-paragraph contract: the Abrahamic covenant (race and population vigor), the Palestinian covenant (geography and property), and the Mosaic covenant (policy — freedom, spiritual life, and establishment). Each paragraph addresses a distinct dimension of client nation existence.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 3. Client nation vigor is always spiritual, never biological or geographical: The Abrahamic covenant demonstrates this through the differential covenant standing of Isaac over Ishmael, Jacob over Esau, and supremely through the supernatural birth of Isaac from Abraham and Sarah at ages 99 and 90. The soul, not the body, is the locus of the factor that makes a people viable as a client nation.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 4. Ultra-supergrace is the mechanism by which the Abrahamic covenant was inaugurated: Abraham and Sarah's maturity adjustment to the justice of God made possible the supernatural provision of a son when every natural capacity had been exhausted. This establishes the pattern: the most critical moments of client nation history depend upon the maturity of specific individuals, not upon the aggregate performance of the population.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 5. The Palestinian covenant establishes the sanctity of property as a theological principle: No client nation can function without defined territory, and no territory can be held without military establishment. The year of Jubilee provision — mandatory restoration of sold property to its owner every fiftieth year — expresses the divine commitment to distributed private ownership as the material basis of freedom.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 6. The full extent of the land grant to Israel awaits the second advent: In the past dispensation Israel held only what its military could conquer and maintain. The boundaries described in Numbers 34 — encompassing the entire Middle East from the Mediterranean and Turkey to the Nile, the Euphrates, and the Trans-Jordan — have never been militarily occupied. Their fulfillment is eschatological, executed by the personal return of the Lord Jesus Christ as God of the armies.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 7. The Decalogue (Codex One of the Mosaic Law) defines freedom, not the totality of sin: Its prohibitions protect property, life, privacy, and the marital covenant. Sin as a theological category vastly exceeds the negative imperatives of the Ten Commandments. The Decalogue's function is to establish the perimeter conditions for a free and ordered society.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 8. The ordinances (Codex Two) constitute a comprehensive Christology in type and shadow: The tabernacle furniture, Levitical offerings, priesthood, and holy days all communicate the person and work of the Lord Jesus Christ. Fulfilled at the cross, these shadows are replaced in the Church Age by the gift of evangelism and the proclamation of the completed work of Christ.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 9. The judgments (Codex Three) provide the establishment policy template for client nation function: Universal military training, fixed-percentage taxation, the sanctity of private property, separation of church and state, and the legitimacy of profit motivation are all embedded in Codex Three. These principles are never set aside, even though the Mosaic Law as a direct legislative code does not apply to Church Age believers or Gentile client nations.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 10. The Mosaic Law cannot justify, sanctify, or produce the Holy Spirit: Romans 3:20, Galatians 2:16, 3:2, 3:21, and Romans 8:3 establish these negatives definitively. The law's function was always the modus operandi of a client nation — the vehicle of freedom within which the spiritual heritage could be perpetuated — never the mechanism of a right standing before God. Patriotism is not salvation.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 11. The five cycles of discipline found in Codex Three still operate in the Church Age: No client nation is exempt from the covenantal consequences of departing from establishment principles. The progressive stages of national divine discipline — economic dysfunction, military defeat, social dissolution, foreign domination, and complete historical destruction — are the inexorable expression of divine justice toward a client nation that has forfeited its function.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Six
text: 12. The current purpose of the Mosaic Law is fourfold for the Church Age believer: It provides a pattern for client nation function (Romans 15:4 context); it is written for the believer's instruction (Romans 15:4); it is written for the believer's example (1 Corinthians 10:11–12); and it establishes the divine standard of reality that any surviving client nation must engage if it is to continue in that capacity.
