Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight

section: Romans 11:25–27 — The Abrahamic, Palestinian, and Mosaic Covenants as the Contract for Client Nation Function
text: Romans 11:25–27 — The Abrahamic, Palestinian, and Mosaic Covenants as the Contract for Client Nation Function

section: Romans 11:25–27 — The Abrahamic, Palestinian, and Mosaic Covenants as the Contract for Client Nation Function
text: Romans 11:25–27 “Lest you be wise in your own sight, I do not want you to be unaware of this mystery, brothers: a partial hardening has come upon Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in. And in this way all Israel will be saved, as it is written, 'The Deliverer will come from Zion, he will banish ungodliness from Jacob'; 'and this will be my covenant with them when I take away their sins.'” (ESV)

section: Romans 11:25–27 — The Abrahamic, Palestinian, and Mosaic Covenants as the Contract for Client Nation Function
text: Corrected translation: For brethren — royal family of God — I do not wish you to be ignorant of this mystery, that you stop being wise in your own estimation. For the hardening in part has happened to Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in. And so all Israel — the saved Jews of the Tribulation — shall be delivered, just as it stands written: He who delivers will come from Zion; He will remove the godless ones from Jacob. Also, this is the covenant to them from Me — from the Lord Jesus Christ, the God of Israel — when I have removed their punishment for sin, the fifth cycle of discipline.

section: Romans 11:25–27 — The Abrahamic, Palestinian, and Mosaic Covenants as the Contract for Client Nation Function
text: These verses establish that a formal contract — the covenant with Israel — governs the entire sweep of Israel's history, her discipline, and her future restoration. That contract is now under examination in detail. The larger context of Romans 11 has traced the mystery of Israel's partial hardening during the Church Age, the fullness of the Gentiles, and the certainty of Israel's future deliverance at the second advent of Christ. This chapter turns to a systematic analysis of the individual covenant paragraphs that compose that contract: the Abrahamic covenant, the Palestinian covenant, and the Mosaic covenant. These paragraphs are not merely antiquarian — their principles govern the existence and function of any client nation to God, including the present Gentile client nation.

section: I. The Abrahamic Covenant — First Paragraph of the Contract
text: I. The Abrahamic Covenant — First Paragraph of the Contract

section: I. The Abrahamic Covenant — First Paragraph of the Contract
text: The contract between God and Israel is structured as a series of covenant paragraphs. The first is the Abrahamic covenant, the foundational grace paragraph in which God as party of the first part made a favorable disposition toward Abraham and his progeny as party of the second part.

section: A. Grace Basis and Racial Vigor
text: A. Grace Basis and Racial Vigor

section: A. Grace Basis and Racial Vigor
text: The Abrahamic covenant is a grace paragraph. Its blessings flow not from any inherent superiority of a people, but from the spiritual factor — the presence of Bible doctrine in the soul and the resulting adjustment to the justice of God. This eliminates any claim of racial determinism as the explanation for national greatness. Vigor in a client nation derives from the soul, not from anthropological classification or genetic composition. The Jewish race was constituted as the first and last specific racial client nation in history, but the principle of spiritual invigoration is transferable: red, yellow, black, and white are equally capable of receiving the divine blessing that flows from spiritual maturity.

section: A. Grace Basis and Racial Vigor
text: The Abrahamic covenant was confirmed to Isaac rather than to his brothers — not on the basis of genetic superiority or maternal heritage, but on the basis of the spiritual factor (Genesis 26:3–4). It was confirmed to Jacob rather than to his twin brother Esau (Genesis 35:12), again not because of physical characteristics but because of the spiritual factor. Members of the same family, even twins, differ decisively on the basis of doctrine intake and volition. Racial or genetic homogeneity has never been the basis of divine blessing.

section: B. Abraham and Sarah — Ultra-Supergrace and Spiritual Prosperity
text: B. Abraham and Sarah — Ultra-Supergrace and Spiritual Prosperity

section: B. Abraham and Sarah — Ultra-Supergrace and Spiritual Prosperity
text: The mechanics of the Abrahamic covenant required spiritual maturity at its very inception. The entire history of the client nation depended at one point upon a man of ninety-nine and a woman of ninety — both well past any natural capacity for the function God required of them. This is the ultra-supergrace pattern: maximum divine blessing channeled through a believer at the peak of spiritual maturity. Sexual prosperity at an age of physical impossibility is the divine authentication of ultra-supergrace status, and from that union came the new race through whom all nations of the earth would be blessed (Genesis 17:8; 22:15–18).

section: B. Abraham and Sarah — Ultra-Supergrace and Spiritual Prosperity
text: Circumcision was introduced in Genesis 17:9–14 as the ritual of confirmation and acknowledgment of the covenant. Ritual is meaningless apart from the doctrinal reality it represents. The circumcision rite was not the substance of the covenant; it pointed to the spiritual factor — the sovereign formation of a new race to serve as God's vehicle for blessing all other nations through the function of the client nation.

section: C. Slavery, Deliverance, and the Spiritual Factor
text: C. Slavery, Deliverance, and the Spiritual Factor

section: C. Slavery, Deliverance, and the Spiritual Factor
text: The covenant was the basis for the divine deliverance of the Jewish people from Egyptian slavery. Four centuries of slavery normally erases a people entirely. Three or four generations of bondage dissolve a population's identity. Yet the Jews emerged from four hundred years of slavery in a single generation and made the transition to nationhood — because the spiritual factor was operative. The survival and reconstitution of Israel is not a sociological phenomenon; it is a theological one, explicable only by the Abrahamic covenant and its grace provisions.

section: D. Summary of the Abrahamic Covenant
text: D. Summary of the Abrahamic Covenant

section: D. Summary of the Abrahamic Covenant
text: The first paragraph of the contract called for a vigorous people — a people animated by principle, capable of self-determination, and sustained by spiritual life rather than by expediency. When spiritual life declines and interlocking systems of arrogance replace doctrinal thinking, national vigor collapses regardless of racial composition, geographic advantage, or inherited wealth. The ultimate blessing in this covenant is declared in Genesis 22:15–18: both the individual imputation of blessing to the mature believer and the corporate blessing of all nations through the function of the client nation.

section: II. The Palestinian Covenant — Second Paragraph of the Contract
text: II. The Palestinian Covenant — Second Paragraph of the Contract

section: II. The Palestinian Covenant — Second Paragraph of the Contract
text: The second paragraph of the contract is the Palestinian covenant, the real estate paragraph. It establishes the geographical dimension of client nation existence. No client nation can function without a defined territorial base; and no territorial base can be maintained without a military establishment capable of gaining and securing it.

section: A. Land, Property, and Freedom
text: A. Land, Property, and Freedom

section: A. Land, Property, and Freedom
text: The sanctity of private property is inseparable from freedom. Where the state owns all property, the people are slaves of the state — a principle visible in every totalitarian system in history. The Palestinian covenant establishes that God has a disposition toward property: people have a right to own it, hold it, and pass it on. Even when property was temporarily forfeited, the Year of Jubilee (every fiftieth year) required its restoration to the original holder, demonstrating that the divine intention is that property remain in the hands of the individual rather than concentrating in the hands of a central authority.

section: A. Land, Property, and Freedom
text: Responsibility in a citizen develops through property ownership and family formation — the two primary structures through which individuals assume accountability beyond themselves. A third instrument for developing responsibility is military service, which trains submission to legitimate authority. The book of Numbers — whose Hebrew title literally refers to those who were mustered or enrolled — is the foundational text for universal military training as national policy. The census of Numbers was a military census; the entire organizational structure described there is a structure for fielding and sustaining a national army.

section: B. Military Function and Property
text: B. Military Function and Property

section: B. Military Function and Property
text: In the ancient world there was no distinction between the military that gained property and the police function that maintained order within it; both were one institution. In every age, no nation can hold more territory than its military establishment can gain and defend. This is the operational principle of the Palestinian covenant in its historical dimension: what Israel could conquer and hold by arms constituted her actual land grant during the Old Testament period. The peak of that territorial extent was reached under Solomon; from that point the decline was continuous, driven by the spiritual factor — specifically by the abandonment of doctrine and the resulting divine discipline.

section: C. The Future Fulfillment — Millennial Land Grant
text: C. The Future Fulfillment — Millennial Land Grant

section: C. The Future Fulfillment — Millennial Land Grant
text: The Palestinian covenant contains a land grant that Israel has never fully possessed, because its complete fulfillment awaits the second advent and the millennial reign of Jesus Christ. The grant was first stated in general terms in Genesis 13:14–15 and Genesis 15:18, confirmed to Isaac (Genesis 26:3–4), reconfirmed to Jacob (Genesis 35:12), reiterated to Moses (Exodus 6:2–8), described with specific boundaries by Moses in Numbers 34:1–12, and prophesied as a future millennial fulfillment by both Moses (Deuteronomy 31–9) and the prophets (Jeremiah 32:36–44; Ezekiel 11:16–21; 36:21–38).

section: C. The Future Fulfillment — Millennial Land Grant
text: The geographical extent of the millennial land grant, as recoverable from the relevant texts interpreted in light of the political geography of Moses' day, includes: the Mediterranean coast as the western border; the land of the Hittites — encompassing what is now central and western Turkey, with the Dardanelles as a plausible northwestern boundary — as the northwestern limit; the Nile River as the southern border, incorporating portions of Egypt and Ethiopia; the Euphrates River as the northeastern border; and Transjordan and Iraq as the eastern boundary. This grant encompasses the entire Middle East — territory including portions of modern Egypt, Ethiopia, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Iraq, southern Iran, southeastern Turkey, and the Sinai. Israel has never occupied this territory in its entirety. Its fulfillment is strictly eschatological, contingent upon the personal reign of the Lord Jesus Christ, at which time the military establishment will no longer be the mechanism of land acquisition. The swords-into-plowshares prophecy of Isaiah 2 is a millennial reality, not a present political program.

section: III. The Mosaic Covenant — Third Paragraph of the Contract
text: III. The Mosaic Covenant — Third Paragraph of the Contract

section: III. The Mosaic Covenant — Third Paragraph of the Contract
text: The third paragraph of the contract is the Mosaic covenant, also called the Mosaic Law. This is the divine paragraph dealing with client nation policy across three domains: freedom, spiritual life, and establishment. Its specific recipient was the nation Israel (Exodus 19:3; Leviticus 26:46; Romans 3:19; 9:4); it was not given to Gentile nations in its totality (Romans 2:12–14), and it was not given to the Church (Acts 15:5, 24; Romans 6:14; Galatians 2:19). Nevertheless, its principles remain applicable to any client nation to God, and it has been preserved in Scripture for the believer's instruction (Romans 15:4) and example (1 Corinthians 10:11–12).

section: A. Codex One — The Decalogue
text: A. Codex One — The Decalogue

section: A. Codex One — The Decalogue
text: The Ten Commandments are the first codex of the Mosaic Law. Their function is frequently misunderstood: they do not define the full scope of sin — sin is a far broader category treated throughout Scripture — but rather define freedom in terms of morality, privacy, property, and authority. The prohibition against theft establishes the principle of private property. The prohibition against murder protects the individual's volition and physical existence. The prohibition against adultery protects the integrity of the marriage institution. The commandment to love God with all the heart and soul establishes that only from a proper orientation to divine authority can establishment function proceed with right motivation. The decalogue thus defines the negative boundaries of freedom in a client nation, not a comprehensive taxonomy of sin.

section: B. Codex Two — The Ordinances
text: B. Codex Two — The Ordinances

section: B. Codex Two — The Ordinances
text: The second codex consists of the ordinances — the spiritual code of the Mosaic Law. This codex defines the spiritual heritage of Israel: the tabernacle and temple structure, the Levitical priesthood, the holy days, and above all the Levitical offerings. Each of these is a shadow pointing to the Lord Jesus Christ, who is their fulfillment. The complete Christology and soteriology of the Old Testament was taught through these ritual systems and through oral communication. Spiritual heritage cannot be transmitted biologically; it requires regeneration — the new birth — and the ongoing intake of doctrine. This is why the pivot of mature believers is indispensable: without regenerate, doctrinally advancing believers, there is no spiritual heritage to perpetuate and no client nation function to sustain.

section: B. Codex Two — The Ordinances
text: The Levitical sacrifices communicated salvation by means of blood — the blood of animals as the dedication of shadows (Hebrews 9:18–22; 10:1). These shadows are fulfilled in Christ and have been set aside. In the present dispensation, personal and corporate evangelism serve the communicative function formerly served by the sacrificial system (Hebrews 9:12–13).

section: C. Codex Three — The Judgments
text: C. Codex Three — The Judgments

section: C. Codex Three — The Judgments
text: The third codex is the establishment code — the judgments. This codex addresses every principle of client nation modus operandi: freedom, privacy, marriage law, military policy, legitimate taxation, diet and health, sanitation and quarantine, the control of crime (including the laws of jurisprudence — apprehension, trial, evidence, and punishment), and the function of free enterprise with profit as a legitimate and protected motive.

section: C. Codex Three — The Judgments
text: Taxation in Codex Three is structured on a fixed-percentage basis — ten percent — which is the equitable and constitutionally sound principle for national revenue: a flat rate applied uniformly, without penalizing productivity. Windfall taxation and confiscatory progressive taxation are contrary to the establishment principles of Codex Three. Redistribution of wealth — the forcible transfer of legitimately acquired property from productive citizens to non-productive ones — is an anti-establishment policy condemned by the very structure of Codex Three.

section: C. Codex Three — The Judgments
text: Codex Three also authorizes the separation of church and state: the Levitical priesthood functions independently of the civil government. This separation is not hostile to religion but protective of it — and of freedom. The sacred building (tabernacle, then temple) is authorized as a community property devoted to worship and doctrinal instruction, exempt from taxation, a principle carried forward legitimately into the present dispensation under the concept of the church building.

section: C. Codex Three — The Judgments
text: Codex Three explicitly rejects revolution and the use of violence against legitimate establishment authority. It equally rejects the socialist premise that men are born equal in capacity or outcome. The equality it establishes is equality before the law and equality of opportunity within a system of freedom — not equality of result.

section: D. What the Mosaic Law Cannot Do
text: D. What the Mosaic Law Cannot Do

section: D. What the Mosaic Law Cannot Do
text: The Mosaic Law cannot justify the sinner before God (Romans 3:20; 3:28; Galatians 2:16; Philippians 3:9). It cannot impart eternal life (Galatians 3:21). It cannot provide the Holy Spirit (Galatians 3:2). It cannot solve the problem of the old sin nature (Romans 8:3). Its purpose is not soteriological but operational: it establishes the modus operandi of the client nation in the temporal and spiritual realms. Patriotism is not salvation. Obedience to establishment law is not spirituality. The law provides the vehicle of freedom within which the spiritual heritage can be perpetuated; it does not constitute that heritage.

section: E. The Setting Aside of the Mosaic Law
text: E. The Setting Aside of the Mosaic Law

section: E. The Setting Aside of the Mosaic Law
text: The Mosaic Law has been set aside in two senses. First, by fulfillment: the Lord Jesus Christ on the cross fulfilled every shadow of the ordinances — the Levitical offerings, the priesthood, the holy days (Matthew 5:17; Romans 10:4). Second, by dispensational transition: it no longer governs believers or the Church as a covenant code (Romans 6:14; Galatians 2:19). However, it has never been set aside in principle as the pattern for client nation existence. The five cycles of discipline, universal military training, the sanctity of property, and the fixed-percentage tax — these principles remain operative for any nation that occupies the role of client nation to God.

section: E. The Setting Aside of the Mosaic Law
text: In summary, the purpose of the Mosaic Law for the present era is fourfold: (1) a pattern for Gentile client nation function in areas of freedom, military, taxation, government, and free enterprise; (2) written instruction for believers (Romans 15:4); (3) written example for believers (1 Corinthians 10:11–12); and (4) a divine standard for establishing reality in a client nation — the grounding in principle without which no national entity can perpetuate its function under God.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight
text: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight
text: 1. The Abrahamic covenant is a grace paragraph. All blessing from God to Abraham, to the Jewish race, and through Israel to the nations flows through divine grace — specifically through the justice of God satisfied by the spiritual factor operative in the client nation. No race is inherently superior; vigor comes from the soul, not from genetics or geography.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight
text: 2. Ultra-supergrace is the pattern for the Abrahamic covenant's fulfillment. The supernatural birth of Isaac through a couple of advanced age demonstrates that the provisions of the covenant are not activated by human capacity but by the maturity adjustment to the justice of God. The ultra-supergrace believer is the mechanism through whom God authenticates His covenant promises.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight
text: 3. The confirmation of the covenant followed the spiritual factor, not the birth order or racial composition. The covenant passed to Isaac over his brothers, and to Jacob over Esau, because of the spiritual factor — volition toward doctrine — not because of genetic or physical characteristics. This principle eliminates racial determinism as a theological category.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight
text: 4. The Palestinian covenant establishes that no client nation can exist without territorial integrity secured by military force. Property is the material basis of freedom. Freedom is the environment required for evangelism, spiritual growth, and missionary function. Military establishment is the instrument that gains and maintains the territorial base. These three — property, freedom, and military — form an inseparable triad in the Palestinian covenant.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight
text: 5. The full extent of the Palestinian land grant awaits the millennial reign of Christ. What Israel possessed historically was only what could be taken and held by arms. The complete land grant — encompassing the entire Middle East from the Nile to the Euphrates and from the Mediterranean to the Transjordan — is eschatological, contingent upon the return of the Lord Jesus Christ as the God of armies.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight
text: 6. The Mosaic Law is structured as three codices serving distinct functions. Codex One (the Decalogue) defines freedom; Codex Two (the Ordinances) communicates the spiritual heritage through Christological shadows; Codex Three (the Judgments) establishes the operational policy of the client nation in every domain of civil life.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight
text: 7. The Decalogue defines freedom, not the totality of sin. The Ten Commandments establish the negative boundaries of freedom — protecting property, life, marriage, and the authority of God — not a comprehensive definition of what constitutes sin. Sin is a far broader category addressed throughout the canon.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight
text: 8. Spiritual heritage is perpetuated by regeneration and doctrine intake, not by physical birth. The ordinances of Codex Two — sacrifice, priesthood, tabernacle, holy days — all pointed to Christ and communicated salvation and spiritual life. In the present dispensation, evangelism and Bible doctrine teaching serve that perpetuating function. Without a regenerate pivot advancing in doctrine, no client nation can sustain its spiritual heritage.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight
text: 9. The Mosaic Law cannot justify, cannot impart eternal life, and cannot solve the old sin nature problem. Its purpose is operational, not soteriological. It provides the vehicle of freedom within which the spiritual heritage is transmitted; it does not constitute that heritage. Patriotism is not salvation, and establishment law-keeping is not spirituality.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Eight
text: 10. The establishment principles of the Mosaic Law remain operative for client nations today. Though the ceremonial and judicial specifics of the Mosaic covenant have been set aside dispensationally, the underlying principles — the five cycles of discipline, universal military training, fixed-percentage taxation, the sanctity of property, the separation of church and state, and the free enterprise system — continue to govern any nation functioning as a client nation to God.

text: A national entity chosen by God to serve as the vehicle for evangelism, missionary activity, and the perpetuation of Bible doctrine in a given historical period. Israel was the original and primary client nation; Gentile nations have served in this role during the times of the Gentiles.

It establishes a new race through Abraham, defines the Jewish people as citizens of the first and last racial client nation, and promises blessing to all nations through Abraham's spiritual seed. Confirmed to Isaac (Genesis 26:3–4) and to Jacob (Genesis 35:12).

section: Romans 11:26–27 · God's Covenant with Israel · The Davidic Covenant and Its Fulfillment · The New Covenant to Israel
text: Romans 11:26–27 · God's Covenant with Israel · The Davidic Covenant and Its Fulfillment · The New Covenant to Israel

section: Romans 11:26–27 · God's Covenant with Israel · The Davidic Covenant and Its Fulfillment · The New Covenant to Israel
text: Romans 11:26–27 “And in this way all Israel will be saved, as it is written, 'The Deliverer will come from Zion, he will banish ungodliness from Jacob'; 'and this will be my covenant with them when I take away their sins.'” (ESV)

section: Romans 11:26–27 · God's Covenant with Israel · The Davidic Covenant and Its Fulfillment · The New Covenant to Israel
text: Corrected translation: And so all Israel shall be delivered, just as it stands written: He who delivers will come from Zion; He will remove the godless ones from Jacob. Also this is the covenant to them from Me, when I have removed their punishment for sin.

section: Romans 11:26–27 · God's Covenant with Israel · The Davidic Covenant and Its Fulfillment · The New Covenant to Israel
text: Romans 11 continues its exposition of God's unbroken covenant relationship with the nation of Israel. Verses 26 and 27 bring into focus the contractual framework that undergirds the entire future of Israel — a framework grounded in the Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, and new covenants. The question posed in verse 1 — has God cast off His people? — is answered definitively in these verses: not now, not ever. This chapter examines the structure of that contract, the problems that arose in its fulfillment, and the doctrines by which each problem is resolved.

section: I. The Contract with Client Nation Israel: Review of the Framework
text: I. The Contract with Client Nation Israel: Review of the Framework

section: I. The Contract with Client Nation Israel: Review of the Framework
text: Verse 27 cites the new covenant to Israel as confirmation that God has not set aside His people. To understand the force of that citation, the full structure of the divine contract with Israel must be held in view. That contract is not a single document but an interlocking series of covenants, each addressing a distinct dimension of the divine-human relationship.

section: The Abrahamic Covenant: The Race
text: The Abrahamic Covenant: The Race

section: The Abrahamic Covenant: The Race
text: The Abrahamic covenant designated the specific race involved in the contract. The Jewish people emerged as a distinct racial entity beginning with Abraham, and this covenant established their unique identity and divine election. The Abrahamic covenant forms the first paragraph of God's contract with Israel.

section: The Palestinian Covenant: The Geography
text: The Palestinian Covenant: The Geography

section: The Palestinian Covenant: The Geography
text: The real estate clause of the contract defined the borders of the promised land with precision: the Mediterranean Sea to the west, the Euphrates River to the north, the Nile to the south (including eastern Egypt and eastern Ethiopia), and Trans-Jordan and Iraq to the east. Western Turkey, identified with the territory of the Hittites, also falls within these boundaries.

section: The Palestinian Covenant: The Geography
text: When Joshua led Israel into the land — the covenant having been reiterated in Joshua 1:2–4 — the operative principle was that Israel would possess as much of that land as it could conquer and hold by military force. This was not a limitation on the covenant but the divinely prescribed mechanism for its current-age implementation. The full extent of the land grant awaits the second advent, when the Lord Jesus Christ as sovereign ruler will bestow on Israel the entire Middle East — including Saudi Arabia, Trans-Jordan, Iraq, Iran, and Turkey — without any military prerequisite, as an act of sovereign grace.

section: The Palestinian Covenant: The Geography
text: The Palestinian covenant thus establishes two distinct phases of fulfillment: the military phase operative during the dispensation of Israel and the present era, and the messianic phase to be inaugurated at the second advent. The millennial promise of Isaiah — that swords will be beaten into plowshares and nations will learn war no more — is strictly applicable to the millennium; there is no military establishment in that age, because the Lord Himself secures the land and its borders.

section: The Mosaic Law: Freedom, Establishment, and the Spiritual Code
text: The Mosaic Law: Freedom, Establishment, and the Spiritual Code

section: The Mosaic Law: Freedom, Establishment, and the Spiritual Code
text: The covenant to Moses organizes the law into three functional codes. Codex One is the freedom code, consisting of the Decalogue. Its provisions — prohibitions against theft, murder, false witness — establish the legal foundation for the three irreducible conditions of freedom: privacy, property, and the voluntary acceptance of legitimate authority.

section: The Mosaic Law: Freedom, Establishment, and the Spiritual Code
text: Freedom is legitimate self-determination: the environment in which human volition operates without arbitrary constraint. It does not manufacture equality; it guarantees inequality, because individuals exercise their freedom differently. The forced redistribution of wealth, confiscatory taxation, and state interference in legitimate private enterprise are each violations of the freedom code. Codex One and Codex Three — the establishment code — have never been abrogated. Only Codex Two, the Levitical sacrificial system, was fulfilled and set aside by the death, burial, and resurrection of Christ.

section: The Mosaic Law: Freedom, Establishment, and the Spiritual Code
text: Codex Three, the establishment code, governs the practical functioning of a client nation: taxation, hygiene, health, sanitation, quarantine, military procedures, and the full range of civil and social order. Any nation operating under these principles — believer and unbeliever alike — benefits from the divinely authorized framework for national stability. Any nation that abandons them moves toward the cycles of divine discipline.

section: The Mosaic Law: Freedom, Establishment, and the Spiritual Code
text: Authority is the essential counterpart to freedom. Freedom without authority is anarchy; authority without freedom is tyranny. Freedom without the authority of doctrine produces antinomianism; authority without freedom produces legalism. The umbrella of authority — delegated by God to family, employer, civil government, and military — is the structural principle by which freedom is sustained rather than destroyed.

section: II. The Davidic Covenant: Point Seven of the Contract
text: II. The Davidic Covenant: Point Seven of the Contract

section: II. The Davidic Covenant: Point Seven of the Contract
text: The seventh point in the contract with Israel is the Davidic covenant, recorded in 2 Samuel 7:8–17 and celebrated in Psalm 89:20–37. God as party of the first part makes a gracious disposition to David as party of the second part: David will have a son who will reign forever over Israel. This is a supergrace blessing to David, and its fulfillment required the resolution of several major doctrinal problems.

section: The Two Lines of Descent
text: The Two Lines of Descent

section: The Two Lines of Descent
text: The Davidic dynasty continued for approximately 400 years in the southern kingdom of Judah (c. 1010–586 BC) and for roughly 72 years over the northern kingdom (c. 998–926 BC). Neither period constitutes the ultimate fulfillment of the covenant. The covenant is fulfilled in the Lord Jesus Christ.

section: The Two Lines of Descent
text: Two sons of David and Bathsheba are critical to the fulfillment: Solomon, the elder, and Nathan, the younger (1 Chronicles 3:5; Luke 3:31). Solomon's line produced the royal dynasty; Nathan's line runs through the Virgin Mary. The distinction between these two lines resolves the central genealogical problem of the Davidic covenant.

section: The Curse on Coniah
text: The Curse on Coniah

section: The Curse on Coniah
text: In the line of Solomon, the king Jehoiakim — second son of Josiah and vassal of Nebuchadnezzar following the battle of Carchemish — was a confirmed reversionist who not only rejected Bible doctrine but destroyed copies of the Scripture. He died under the sin unto death, as prophesied in Jeremiah 36:29–31.

section: The Curse on Coniah
text: His son Coniah (also called Jeconiah or Jehoiachin) ruled from 597 BC for only three months and ten days before Nebuchadnezzar returned and took him into captivity, where he remained a prisoner for 86 years. Upon Coniah the following curse was pronounced in Jeremiah 22:28–30:

section: The Curse on Coniah
text: Jeremiah 22:28–30 “Is this man Coniah a despised, broken pot, a vessel no one cares for? Why are he and his children hurled and cast into a land that they do not know? O land, land, land, hear the word of the LORD! Thus says the LORD: 'Write this man down as childless, a man who shall not succeed in his days, for none of his offspring shall succeed in sitting on the throne of David and ruling again in Judah.'” (ESV)

section: The Curse on Coniah
text: Corrected translation: Is this man Coniah a shattered jar, or an undesirable vessel? Why have he and his descendants been hurled out and cast into a land which they have not known? Thus says the LORD: Write this man down as childless, a man who will not prosper in his days, for no man of his descendants will prosper sitting on the throne of David.

section: The Curse on Coniah
text: The curse meant that although Solomon's line continued to produce descendants, no member of that line could legitimately occupy David's throne in fulfillment of the covenant. The line terminates with Joseph, who is the legal but not the biological father of the humanity of Christ. Matthew's genealogy traces the legal line through Joseph, descended from David through Solomon and Coniah (Matthew 1:1–17). This establishes the legal right to the Davidic throne.

section: The Curse on Coniah
text: Luke's genealogy traces the biological line through Mary, descended from David through Nathan (Luke 3:23–38). Because Joseph was not the real father of the Lord Jesus Christ — the virgin birth being the mechanism by which the Holy Spirit bypassed the Solomonic-Conianic line — the curse is perfectly fulfilled: no son of Coniah sits on David's throne. The throne passes instead through the Nathanic line via Mary.

section: The Curse on Coniah
text: The virgin birth simultaneously accomplishes two things: it fulfills the curse on Coniah, and it prevents the imputation of Adam's original sin and the transmission of the old sin nature through the male genetic line, preserving the impeccability of the humanity of Christ.

section: Problems in the Fulfillment and Their Doctrinal Resolutions
text: Problems in the Fulfillment and Their Doctrinal Resolutions

section: Problems in the Fulfillment and Their Doctrinal Resolutions
text: The fulfillment of the Davidic covenant encountered a series of problems, each of which is resolved by a foundational doctrine of the Christian faith.

section: Problems in the Fulfillment and Their Doctrinal Resolutions
text: Problem 1: The physical death of Christ. If Christ is the fulfillment of the Davidic covenant — the Son who reigns forever — how can the covenant be fulfilled when He has died? The resolution is the bodily, physical resurrection of Christ. As Paul states in Romans 1:3–4 and alludes to in 2 Timothy 2:8 and Acts 26:6–8, the resurrection is the direct answer to the problem of physical death in the fulfillment of the covenant.

section: Problems in the Fulfillment and Their Doctrinal Resolutions
text: Problem 2: The removal of Israel as a client nation. In AD 70, Israel went out under the fifth cycle of discipline. The insertion of the church age and the times of the Gentiles meant that only Gentile nations could function as client nations to God during this intercalated dispensation. How can David's Son reign over Israel if Israel is not a client nation? The resolution is the ascension and session of Christ, who currently reigns at the right hand of the Father as King of kings and Lord of lords, and the certainty of the second advent, at which point Israel will be restored.

section: Problems in the Fulfillment and Their Doctrinal Resolutions
text: Problem 3: The destruction of the universe. Can the eternal reign of David's Son be reconciled with the prophesied destruction of the present heavens and earth? The relevant passages — Isaiah 34, 2 Peter 3:10, 12, and Revelation 20–21 — do speak of the destruction and recreation of the universe. However, this destruction does not occur until after the millennium — after 1,000 years of the reign of Christ — and is followed immediately by the new heavens and the new earth. Isaiah 66:22 states: “For just as the new heavens and the new earth which I will make will stand before Me,” declares the LORD, “so your offspring and your name will stand.” The eternal covenant with Israel is not undone by the destruction of the present universe; it carries into the eternal state.

section: III. The New Covenant to Israel: Point Eight of the Contract
text: III. The New Covenant to Israel: Point Eight of the Contract

section: III. The New Covenant to Israel: Point Eight of the Contract
text: The eighth and final point in God's contract with Israel is the new covenant, recorded in Jeremiah 31:31–34. This covenant is cited directly in Romans 11:27 as confirmation that God has not cast off His people.

section: III. The New Covenant to Israel: Point Eight of the Contract
text: The new covenant is the divine promise to a dispersed and disciplined Israel that they will be restored as a client nation to God at the second advent. The restored client nation will continue forever — both through the millennium (the last 1,000 years of human history under the messianic reign) and into the eternal state. Jeremiah anticipates both the removal of Israel as a client nation (Jeremiah 31:31–32) and their restoration (Jeremiah 31:33–34).

section: III. The New Covenant to Israel: Point Eight of the Contract
text: The new covenant functions as a link between the Mosaic law and the millennial restoration. It does not replace the Abrahamic, Palestinian, or Davidic covenants; it reiterates and confirms them. The millennium — which may be called the dispensation of the second client-ship of Israel — operates under the full terms of the original contract, now designated the new covenant, with the refinements appropriate to the messianic age.

section: III. The New Covenant to Israel: Point Eight of the Contract
text: The insertion of the church age does not alter Israel's future. It provides a royal family for the Lord Jesus Christ as King of kings and Lord of lords, and it establishes the mechanism by which Gentile nations become client nations to God through the pivot of mature believers within them. But the removal of Israel as a client nation in AD 70, and the insertion of the times of the Gentiles, sets aside only that portion of the Mosaic law that pertained to the sacrificial system fulfilled at the cross. The establishment and freedom codes remain operative for any client nation.

section: IV. The Correct Translation of Romans 11:25–27
text: IV. The Correct Translation of Romans 11:25–27

section: IV. The Correct Translation of Romans 11:25–27
text: With the full covenantal framework in view, the correct translation of verses 25 through 27 may now be rendered as follows:

section: IV. The Correct Translation of Romans 11:25–27
text: Verse 25: For, brethren — royal family of God — I do not wish you to be ignorant of this mystery, lest you become wise in your own estimation: that hardening in part has happened to Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in.

section: IV. The Correct Translation of Romans 11:25–27
text: The hardening in part — the judicial hardening of a portion of Israel as a consequence of sustained negative volition toward the gospel — is the basis for the periodic historical cycles of persecution that have fallen upon the Jewish people. This hardening is not permanent and is not total. It continues only until the fullness of the Gentiles — the completion of the church age — has come in.

section: IV. The Correct Translation of Romans 11:25–27
text: Verse 26: And so all Israel shall be delivered, just as it stands written: He who delivers will come from Zion; He will remove the godless ones from Jacob.

section: IV. The Correct Translation of Romans 11:25–27
text: The quotation is from Isaiah 59:20–21 and Isaiah 27:9. The deliverance of all Israel is eschatological — it takes place at the second advent of Christ, at the end of the tribulation. The removal of the godless ones from Jacob refers to the baptism of fire, by which unbelieving Jews and Gentiles are excluded from entering the millennium.

section: IV. The Correct Translation of Romans 11:25–27
text: Verse 27: Also this is the covenant to them — to Jewish believers of the millennium — from Me, from Jesus Christ the God of Israel, when I have removed their punishment for sin.

section: IV. The Correct Translation of Romans 11:25–27
text: The punishment for sin is not sin itself but the fifth cycle of discipline — the historical judgment that has attended Israel's dispersion from AD 70 onward. The removal of the fifth cycle at the second advent inaugurates Israel's restoration as a client nation and the fulfillment of the new covenant.

section: V. The Governing Question: Has God Cast Off His People?
text: V. The Governing Question: Has God Cast Off His People?

section: V. The Governing Question: Has God Cast Off His People?
text: The entire argument of Romans 11 is an extended answer to the question of verse 1: has God forsaken His people? The survey of the covenantal contract — Abrahamic, Palestinian, Mosaic, Davidic, new — gives the definitive answer: absolutely not. Each problem that arose in the fulfillment of the covenant was resolved by a foundational doctrine: the virgin birth, the impeccability of Christ, the resurrection, the ascension and session, the second advent, and the eternal new creation.

section: V. The Governing Question: Has God Cast Off His People?
text: Anti-Semitism in any form — whether the murderous variety that originated in Eastern Europe and found its ultimate expression in the Third Reich, or the ideological variety circulated in ostensibly conservative political literature — represents a direct assault on the divine contract. It is both historically catastrophic and theologically incoherent. The divine commitment to Israel, sealed in covenant across four millennia, cannot be annulled by any human or satanic agency. Isaiah 66:22 stands: Israel's seed and Israel's name will stand as long as the new heavens and the new earth stand before the face of the LORD.

section: V. The Governing Question: Has God Cast Off His People?
text: For the church age believer, the covenantal heritage of Israel is not merely historical background — it is the spiritual inheritance of the royal family of God. The same God who maintains His contract with Israel maintains His new covenant with the church. The pivot of mature believers in any Gentile client nation is the functional counterpart to the covenant-keeping remnant within Israel. God's faithfulness to His people in any dispensation is grounded in the same immutable character of divine justice and grace.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine
text: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine
text: 1. The contract with Israel is multi-covenantal. It consists of at least eight interlocking covenants — Abrahamic, Palestinian, Mosaic (three codices), Davidic, and new — each addressing a distinct dimension of the divine-human relationship. No single covenant can be understood in isolation from the others.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine
text: 2. The Palestinian covenant operates on a military principle in the current age. Israel possesses only what it can hold through its military establishment. The full land grant awaits the second advent, when the Lord Jesus Christ will bestow the entire Middle East on Israel as an act of sovereign grace, without any military prerequisite.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine
text: 3. Freedom requires three structural conditions: privacy, property, and voluntary acceptance of authority. The removal of any one of these produces either anarchy or tyranny. The freedom code of the Mosaic law establishes these conditions as divinely authorized principles operative for any client nation, believer and unbeliever alike.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine
text: 4. The Davidic covenant is fulfilled in the Lord Jesus Christ through the resolution of four specific problems. The virgin birth resolves the curse on Coniah and preserves impeccability. The resurrection resolves physical death. The ascension and session resolve the removal of Israel as a client nation. The second advent resolves the gap between the present age and the millennial reign.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine
text: 5. The curse on Coniah (Jeremiah 22:28–30) required the virgin birth. No biological son of Coniah could sit on David's throne. The Lord Jesus Christ, whose legal genealogy runs through Joseph and the Solomonic-Conianic line (Matthew 1), and whose biological genealogy runs through Mary and the Nathanic line (Luke 3), fulfills the covenant without violating the curse.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine
text: 6. The so-called doomsday passages (Isaiah 34; 2 Peter 3:10, 12; Revelation 20–21) refer to events at the end of the millennium, not to any current or near-term catastrophe. The destruction of the present universe is followed immediately by the new heavens and the new earth, in which the eternal covenant with Israel — and with the church — continues without interruption.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine
text: 7. The new covenant to Israel (Jeremiah 31:31–34) is not a replacement of the prior covenants but their reiteration and confirmation. It links the Mosaic law to the millennial restoration and guarantees the perpetuation of Israel as a client nation — both in time (the millennium) and in eternity. This is the covenant cited in Romans 11:27 as the definitive answer to the question of whether God has cast off His people.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine
text: 8. The insertion of the church age does not alter Israel's future. The church age provides a royal family for Christ as King of kings and Lord of lords and establishes Gentile client nations through the pivot of mature believers. The times of the Gentiles sets aside only Codex Two of the Mosaic law — the sacrificial system fulfilled at the cross. Codex One (freedom code) and Codex Three (establishment code) remain operative for any client nation in any dispensation.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine
text: 9. Anti-Semitism is incompatible with the divine contract and with orthodox Christian theology. The divine commitment to Israel is sealed across four millennia of covenantal history and confirmed in Romans 11:26–27. Any ideological system, political movement, or religious tradition that targets the Jewish people as a race stands in direct opposition to the character of God as expressed in His word and His covenants.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Forty-Nine
text: 10. Romans 11:26–27 answers the governing question of the chapter with covenantal finality. God has not cast off His people. The hardening in part is temporary — it continues only until the fullness of the Gentiles is complete. At the second advent, all Israel shall be delivered, the fifth cycle of discipline will be removed, and the new covenant will be fully inaugurated. The study continues in verse 28.

section: Glossary

Codex Two: the spiritual code (Levitical sacrificial system, fulfilled and abrogated by the cross). Codex Three: the establishment code (civil, military, hygiene, taxation, and social order — never abrogated, operative for any client nation).

section: Romans 11:28 — The Two Elections: Israel and the Church; Covenant Status in the Church Age
text: Romans 11:28 — The Two Elections: Israel and the Church; Covenant Status in the Church Age

section: Romans 11:28 — The Two Elections: Israel and the Church; Covenant Status in the Church Age
text: Romans 11:28 “As regards the gospel, they are enemies for your sake. But as regards election, they are beloved for the sake of their forefathers.” (ESV)

section: Romans 11:28 — The Two Elections: Israel and the Church; Covenant Status in the Church Age
text: Corrected translation: On the one hand, with reference to the gospel, they — Jewish unbelievers — are regarded as enemies because of you, the church as a special election to privilege. But on the other hand, as far as their election is concerned, they — Jewish believers — are beloved because of their fathers, Israel as a special election to privilege.

section: Romans 11:28 — The Two Elections: Israel and the Church; Covenant Status in the Church Age
text: Having completed the exposition of verse 27 — the covenant Christ will fulfill at the second advent by removing the fifth cycle of discipline from Israel — the commentary now moves to verse 28. This verse introduces a compressed but theologically dense contrast between two categories: the Jewish unbeliever of the church age, who stands in enmity toward God through rejection of the gospel, and the Jewish believer of the dispensation of Israel, who was beloved through election to privilege under the covenants. The verse operates within the framework of classical Greek correlative particles and demands careful grammatical unpacking before its doctrinal content can be stated precisely.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: Before the grammar of verse 28 can be exegeted, a foundational question must be answered: what covenant or contract governs Jew and Gentile during the period when Israel is out under the fifth cycle of discipline? The answer is the new covenant to the church — a contract that supersedes all of the Jewish covenants without destroying the continuity of spiritual heritage.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: The relevant Scripture for the new covenant to the church includes Matthew 26:28, Mark 14:24, Luke 22:20, 1 Corinthians 11:25, 2 Corinthians 3:6, Hebrews 7:22, Hebrews 9:15–20, Hebrews 10:29, and Hebrews 12:24. These citations together authorize a new contract during the time when national Israel, as a client nation and as God's people in a dispensational sense, is under divine discipline.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: Thirteen structural features define this new covenant to the church and establish the context for reading verse 28:

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: 1. God as party of the first part makes a gracious disposition in favor of party of the second part. In this dispensation, party of the second part is not a nation such as Israel, but any Gentile client nation and, within it, the body of believers known as the royal family of God, composed of Jewish and Gentile believers alike.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: 2. The new covenant to the church supersedes all of the Jewish covenants without destroying the continuity of spiritual heritage. The heritage passes to the church for the duration of the dispensation.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: 3. The new covenant to the church authorizes a new priesthood: a universal royal priesthood. Every believer in the church age is his own priest. Volition combined with royal priesthood provides everything necessary for fulfillment of the protocol plan of God.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: 4. The new covenant to the church defines both the spiritual heritage of the royal family and the client nation policy of the pivot during the church age and the times of the Gentiles.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: 5. Every Jew and every Gentile who believes in the Lord Jesus Christ enters the royal family of God and, as his own priest, is commanded to function under the honor code of the royal family — the operational standard developed in Romans 12 through 16.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: 6. The new covenant to the church authorizes the election of the royal family of God during the times of the Gentiles to replace Israel as God's covenant people for this dispensation only. The baptism of the Holy Spirit — placing the believer in union with Christ — is the mechanism of entry into this election.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: 7. The new covenant to the church voids temporarily the covenant promises to Israel — Abrahamic, Palestinian, Mosaic, Davidic, and new — for the duration of the church age. These promises remain intact in their original form but are postponed until the second advent and the millennial reign of Christ.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: 8. A distinction must therefore be maintained between the new covenant to the church, pertaining to the dispensation of the church, and the new covenant to Israel, pertaining to the millennial reign of Christ. The former features a universal royal priesthood of all believers; the latter features a specialized priesthood within client nation Israel in the millennium.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: 9. The new covenant to the church establishes the royal family of God forever. The new covenant to Israel establishes Israel as a client nation forever. These are two distinct and permanent institutions.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: 10. Client nation function belonging to Israel is discontinued at A.D. 70 — the fifth cycle of discipline under Titus. From A.D. 70 until the second advent, the only functioning client nations are Gentile client nations sustained by a pivot of mature believers who have received and perpetuated the spiritual heritage once belonging to Israel. That heritage includes not only the gospel of Jesus Christ but the foundational principles of freedom through military victory, property and privacy rights, the laws of divine establishment, and prosperity through free enterprise under limited government.

section: I. Preliminary Framework: The New Covenant to the Church
text: 11. The client nation function of Israel in the millennium is authorized under the new covenant to Israel. The client nation function of Gentile nations such as the United States is authorized under the new covenant to the church. These two authorizations are dispensationally distinct.

section: II. Exegesis of Romans 11:28a — Jewish Unbelievers as Enemies
text: II. Exegesis of Romans 11:28a — Jewish Unbelievers as Enemies

section: A. The Classical Greek Correlative Construction
text: A. The Classical Greek Correlative Construction

section: A. The Classical Greek Correlative Construction
text: Verse 28 opens with a correlative construction drawn from Attic Greek: the affirmative particle men (μέν), followed later by the correlative particle de (δέ). The classical pairing men … de — μέν … δέ — introduces a formal contrast: on the one hand … on the other hand. This construction governs the entire verse and signals that two parallel but contrasting statements are about to be made about Israel.

section: B. The First Clause: With Reference to the Gospel
text: B. The First Clause: With Reference to the Gospel

section: B. The First Clause: With Reference to the Gospel
text: The first prepositional phrase is kata (κατά) plus the accusative singular of euangelion (εὐαγγέλιον), meaning gospel. The preposition kata with the accusative does not mean concerning in the sense of subject matter but rather with reference to — indicating a standard or sphere of evaluation. The corrected translation is therefore: on the one hand, with reference to the gospel.

section: B. The First Clause: With Reference to the Gospel
text: The subject of the first clause is Jewish unbelievers. The verb to be must be supplied from context, giving: with reference to the gospel, they are. The predicate nominative following is derived from the noun:

section: B. The First Clause: With Reference to the Gospel
text: echthos (ἐχθρός): enemy. The form here is nominative plural, functioning as a predicate: they are enemies. This does not mean that God has personal hostility toward unbelieving Jews in the sense of hatred; rather it is an anthropopathism — a divine policy expressed in human relational terms. All unbelievers, whether Jew or Gentile, stand in the status of spiritual death and are therefore in a state of enmity with God. The passage focuses on Jewish unbelievers because of the dispensational context.

section: C. For Your Sake — the Church as the Determining Factor
text: C. For Your Sake — the Church as the Determining Factor

section: C. For Your Sake — the Church as the Determining Factor
text: The phrase di' hymas (δι' ὑμᾶς) — the preposition dia plus the accusative plural of the second person personal pronoun — means because of you or for your sake. The referent is Gentile believers, and by extension the entire royal family of God composed of Jewish and Gentile believers. The corrected translation of the first clause is: On the one hand, with reference to the gospel, they — Jewish unbelievers — are regarded as enemies because of you, the church as a special election to privilege.

section: C. For Your Sake — the Church as the Determining Factor
text: The theological meaning is as follows. God imputed divine righteousness to Abraham at the point of his faith in the Lord Jesus Christ — long before circumcision, long before the Mosaic Law, long before the Jewish race formally existed. That imputed righteousness established the grace pipeline: from the justice of God to the righteousness of God, from one half of divine integrity to the other. This same pattern of justification by faith is now operative in the church age for Gentile believers. For the sake of those Gentile believers — who now possess the righteousness of God through faith in Christ — Jewish unbelievers who reject Christ are classified as enemies of God. No Jewish covenant is operative in the church age that could provide them an alternative standing.

section: C. For Your Sake — the Church as the Determining Factor
text: The Abrahamic covenant is not operative, because there is no Jewish client nation for the Jewish race to function as covenant people. The Palestinian covenant is not operative, because there is no Jewish client nation for the land grant to be administered. The Mosaic Law as client nation policy is not operative, because there is no Jewish client nation for it to govern. The Davidic covenant is not operative, because there is no Jewish client nation over which the dynasty of David and the person of Christ rules. The new covenant to Israel is not operative, because neither a Jewish client nation nor the millennial reign of Christ yet exists.

section: C. For Your Sake — the Church as the Determining Factor
text: The only covenant available to the Jew in the church age is the new covenant to the church — and the prerequisite for entering that covenant is personal faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. When the Jewish unbeliever rejects Christ, he rejects the only contract through which God's plan is currently operating. Outside that contract, Jewish unbelievers, exactly like Gentile unbelievers, stand as enemies of God.

section: III. Exegesis of Romans 11:28b — Jewish Believers as Beloved
text: III. Exegesis of Romans 11:28b — Jewish Believers as Beloved

section: A. The Second Clause: As Far as Their Election Is Concerned
text: A. The Second Clause: As Far as Their Election Is Concerned

section: A. The Second Clause: As Far as Their Election Is Concerned
text: The second clause opens with the post-positive conjunctive particle de (δέ), completing the classical Attic correlative: but on the other hand. This is followed by kata (κατά) plus the accusative singular of eklogē (ἐκλογή): election, selection, choice. Corrected translation of the prepositional phrase: but on the other hand, as far as their election is concerned.

section: B. Beloved — Jewish Believers of the Dispensation of Israel
text: B. Beloved — Jewish Believers of the Dispensation of Israel

section: B. Beloved — Jewish Believers of the Dispensation of Israel
text: The predicate nominative is agapētos (ἀγαπητός): beloved, dear, accepted. The form here is nominative plural. The verb must again be supplied: they are beloved. The referent is the Jewish believers of the dispensation of Israel — not Jewish believers of the church age specifically, though those are included by implication. The term agapētos is a technical term in Pauline usage for the church age believer as one accepted in Christ through positional truth. Here it is applied to Jewish believers of the prior dispensation in terms of their covenant standing.

section: C. Because of the Fathers
text: C. Because of the Fathers

section: C. Because of the Fathers
text: The final phrase is dia tous pateras (διὰ τοὺς πατέρας): because of the fathers. The word pateras refers to the Jewish believers of the dispensation of Israel, with particular emphasis on the patriarchal line: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Jesus Christ is identified as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob because each personally believed in Him. The Jewish race originated through regeneration. The election of the fathers was tied to client nation Israel and to the covenants given to that nation. Those covenants are postponed — not canceled — until the second advent. Because of the fathers, Jewish believers of any age carry the heritage of an election to privilege that is rooted in God's irrevocable purposes.

section: C. Because of the Fathers
text: The full corrected translation of verse 28 reads: On the one hand, with reference to the gospel, they — Jewish unbelievers — are regarded as enemies because of you, body of Christ, the church as a special election to privilege. But on the other hand, as far as their election is concerned, they — Jewish believers — are beloved because of their fathers, Israel as a special election to privilege, client nation.

section: IV. Doctrinal Analysis: Two Elections to Privilege
text: IV. Doctrinal Analysis: Two Elections to Privilege

section: IV. Doctrinal Analysis: Two Elections to Privilege
text: Verse 28 names two categories of election within the protocol plan of God. Each is an election to special privilege. Each is entered through personal faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. Each has a distinct dispensational identity.

section: IV. Doctrinal Analysis: Two Elections to Privilege
text: The first election to privilege is Israel. Its special relationship with God is defined and revealed through the covenants to Israel: the Abrahamic covenant, the Palestinian covenant, the Mosaic covenant, the Davidic covenant, and the new covenant to Israel. These covenants collectively constitute the divine authorization for Israel as a client nation and as God's covenant people during the dispensation of Israel. The election of Israel is expressed through these contractual relationships.

section: IV. Doctrinal Analysis: Two Elections to Privilege
text: The second election to privilege is the church. Its special relationship with God is defined and revealed through the baptism of the Holy Spirit and the resulting positional truth — the placement of every believer in union with Christ at the moment of faith. This is the unique characteristic of the royal family of God in the church age. The election of the church is expressed through this positional union.

section: IV. Doctrinal Analysis: Two Elections to Privilege
text: Both elections share one non-negotiable prerequisite: personal faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. Abraham was justified by faith in Christ prior to circumcision and prior to the Mosaic Law. Every Jewish believer of the Old Testament was justified by the same faith. Every believer in the church age, whether Jew or Gentile, is justified by the same faith. A change in dispensation does not change the way of salvation. The way of salvation is, has always been, and will always be personal faith in the Lord Jesus Christ — non-meritorious, non-ceremonial, and without supplementation of any kind.

section: IV. Doctrinal Analysis: Two Elections to Privilege
text: The contrast in verse 28 is therefore between Jewish unbeliever of the church age — who is outside the only operative covenant by rejection of Christ — and Jewish believer of the dispensation of Israel — who was inside the covenant election of his age through faith in Christ. The similarity is between Jewish believer of the dispensation of Israel and Jewish believer of the church age: both are elected to privilege through faith in Christ, though the dispensational expression of that privilege differs.

section: IV. Doctrinal Analysis: Two Elections to Privilege
text: There are only two groups elected to special privilege in history, aside from the unique person of Jesus Christ whose election as the God-man is in a category entirely its own. Israel and the church are both elected to privilege, but they differ in time, in dispensational function, and in the contractual framework that defines their relationship to God. These distinctions must be maintained with precision. Confusion between Israel and the church at this point generates cascading errors in eschatology, ecclesiology, and soteriology.

section: IV. Doctrinal Analysis: Two Elections to Privilege
text: In the church age, Israel is out under the fifth cycle of discipline. No Jewish covenant is operative. The greatest blessing available to any Jew alive today is to believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, enter the royal family of God through the baptism of the Spirit, advance to maturity through sustained doctrine intake under the grace apparatus for perception, crack the maturity barrier, and become part of the pivot in a functioning Gentile client nation. This is not a lesser status: the Jew who reaches spiritual maturity in the church age is a member of the royal family of God — the highest estate God has ever conferred on any human creature — and participates in the blessing cycle that flows from the justice of God through the righteousness of God to the mature believer.

section: IV. Doctrinal Analysis: Two Elections to Privilege
text: God cannot repudiate or reject His people whom He has foreknown and elected. The question posed in Romans 11:1 — Has God cast away His people? — is answered in this verse. The answer is no. Jewish believers are beloved because of the fathers. Jewish unbelievers remain outside the plan of God through their own rejection of Christ. The issue is always the same: attitude toward the Lord Jesus Christ as the only Savior.

section: V. Romans 11:29 — Introduced
text: V. Romans 11:29 — Introduced

section: V. Romans 11:29 — Introduced
text: The exposition of verse 28 establishes the theological platform for verse 29, which in the King James Version reads: For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance. This translation, while familiar, does not render the Greek with precision. The corrected translation moves in the direction of: For the grace benefits and election from God are irrevocable. Verse 29 will be treated in the following chapter. Its governing claim — that the plan of God operates without failure, without revision, and without regret — follows directly from the two-election framework of verse 28. Because God's plan is perfect, it has perfect security, perfect stability, and perfect consistency for all who are within it.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 1. The correlative construction men … de governs verse 28. The classical Attic pairing on the one hand … on the other hand structures a formal contrast between two categories of Israel: the Jewish unbeliever regarded as an enemy with reference to the gospel, and the Jewish believer regarded as beloved with reference to the election.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 2. Enmity toward God is the status of all who reject Christ, Jew or Gentile. The term enemies is an anthropopathism expressing a divine policy in human relational terms. Jewish unbelievers in the church age are outside every operative covenant and therefore outside the plan of God, exactly as Gentile unbelievers are.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 3. No Jewish covenant is operative during the church age. The Abrahamic, Palestinian, Mosaic, Davidic, and new covenants to Israel are all postponed until the second advent. The only contract currently operative for any person — Jew or Gentile — is the new covenant to the church, whose prerequisite is personal faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 4. The new covenant to the church supersedes the Jewish covenants without canceling them. Supersession is temporary and dispensational, not permanent and ontological. The covenants to Israel remain intact; their administration is deferred until the millennium.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 5. For your sake — dia hymas — identifies the church as the reason for the current dispensational arrangement. Gentile believers who possess the righteousness of God through faith in Christ are the beneficiaries of the present age. Jewish unbelievers, by rejecting Christ, stand outside the only plan God is currently running.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 6. Beloved — agapētos — is a technical term for those within the election to privilege. Applied here to Jewish believers of the dispensation of Israel, it identifies them as standing within the covenant relationship established through the fathers: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, each of whom personally believed in the Lord Jesus Christ.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 7. There are exactly two elections to special privilege in human history: Israel and the church. Israel's election is expressed through the covenants. The church's election is expressed through the baptism of the Holy Spirit and positional truth — union with Christ. Both elections demand personal faith in the Lord Jesus Christ as their non-negotiable entry point.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 8. A change in dispensation does not change the way of salvation. From Abraham forward, through the dispensation of Israel, through the church age, and into the millennium, the means of justification is identical: personal, non-meritorious faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 9. The contrast in verse 28 is dispensational, not racial. Jewish unbelievers of the church age are enemies; Jewish believers of the dispensation of Israel are beloved. The determining factor in both cases is relationship to Christ through faith, not ethnicity, lineage, or religious heritage.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 10. The greatest blessing available to any Jew in the church age is spiritual maturity within the royal family of God. With no Jewish client nation operative and no Jewish covenant active, the Jew who believes in Christ enters the royal family, advances through sustained doctrine intake, cracks the maturity barrier, and participates in the pivot of a Gentile client nation — the highest category of blessing God currently administers.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 11. God has not cast away His people — Romans 11:1 is answered by Romans 11:28. Jewish believers are beloved because of the fathers. The election of Israel stands, deferred but not destroyed. Jewish unbelievers exclude themselves from the plan by their own rejection of Christ, not by any act of divine abandonment.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Seven Hundred Fifty
text: 12. Verse 29 establishes that the grace benefits and election from God are irrevocable. The perfection of the divine plan entails perfect security, perfect stability, and perfect consistency for all who are within it — a claim that will be exegeted in the following chapter.

text: Classical Attic Greek correlative particles introducing a formal contrast between two parallel statements. The men-clause states the first member of the contrast; the de-clause states the correlative member. When used with the accusative in this evaluative sense, kata does not mean 'concerning' (as a topic) but 'with reference to' or 'in the sphere of,' indicating the standard or domain by which something is assessed. Used twice in verse 28: with reference to the gospel; as far as their election is concerned.

text: A figure of speech in which God's actions or policies are described using human emotional or relational categories that do not literally apply to His immutable nature. In Romans 11:28, the classification of Jewish unbelievers as 'enemies' is an anthropopathism: it expresses the divine policy of exclusion from the covenant in terms intelligible to human readers, without implying personal animosity in the divine nature.

This is the unique identifier of the royal family of God in the church age and constitutes the mechanism by which the second election to privilege is entered. Distinguished from water baptism and from any experiential empowerment event.

section: Glossary
text: The maximum stage of national divine discipline, resulting in complete historical destruction of the client nation: military defeat, deportation, and diaspora. Applied to Israel in A.D. 70 under Titus. During this cycle, all Jewish covenants are administratively suspended and Israel functions neither as a client nation nor as God's covenant people in a dispensational sense. The cycle terminates at the second advent of Christ.
