section: Romans 15:11 — Psalm 117 and the Fourth Documentation: Isaiah 11:10 — Christ as Guide-On of the Nations; Gentile Believers in Every Dispensation
text: Romans 15:11 continues Paul's chain of Old Testament citations establishing that Jesus Christ is the minister to Gentiles as well as Jews. The present chapter examines Paul's quotation of Psalm 117 and his fourth and final documentation from Isaiah 11:10, together with the Greek morphology of these quotations and the dispensational and eschatological principles they establish. The analysis brings to completion Paul's case that Gentile believers have always had full standing before God in every period of history — past, present, and future.

section: I. Psalm 117 as the Third Documentation (Romans 15:11a)
text: I. Psalm 117 as the Third Documentation (Romans 15:11a)

section: I. Psalm 117 as the Third Documentation (Romans 15:11a)
text: Paul's quotation in Romans 15:11 draws directly from Psalm 117:1–2. This is the shortest psalm in the canon and stands at the numerical center of the Hebrew Scriptures. Despite its brevity, its theological content is dense: it addresses Gentile believers, calls them to worship, and grounds that worship in grace and doctrine.

section: A. The Verb aineō — Praise as Doctrinal Worship
text: A. The Verb aineō — Praise as Doctrinal Worship

section: A. The Verb aineō — Praise as Doctrinal Worship
text: The imperative in the quotation derives from the present active imperative of aineō (αἰνέω), meaning to praise or to celebrate. In this context it denotes the expression of worship grounded in Bible doctrine resident in the soul. The customary present tense indicates habitual action: the mature believer regularly and characteristically engages in this worship. The active voice identifies the mature Gentile believer as the one producing the action. The imperative mood functions here as an imperative of permission — the command is in compliance with an expressed desire on the part of the one who is its object. The mature believer not only receives the command but is inclined toward its fulfillment by the doctrine already resident in the soul.

section: A. The Verb aineō — Praise as Doctrinal Worship
text: The accusative singular direct object is from Kyrios (κύριος), the battlefield title of royalty applied to the Lord Jesus Christ — King of kings and Lord of lords, compressed into a single word. The generic use of the definite article emphasizes both Christ's third category of royalty and His uniqueness in hypostatic union. The vocative plural of pas (πᾶς) plus ethnos (ἔθνος) — all you Gentiles — is the direct address of the imperative.

section: B. The Verb epaineō — Applaud as Overt Worship
text: B. The Verb epaineō — Applaud as Overt Worship

section: B. The Verb epaineō — Applaud as Overt Worship
text: The second verb in the quotation is from epaineō (ἐπαινέω), formed by the prefix epi- added to aineō. The prefix carries the sense of applauding — an overt, outward manifestation of an inward attitude. The English rendering "laud" (from the Old English via Latin) captures the sense. The combinative aorist tense views the worship in its entirety but regards it from the viewpoint of existing results — the mature believer applauds. The active voice again identifies the mature Gentile believer as the subject. The imperative of permission applies as before: the command is in compliance with the believer's own manifest inclination, involving both consent and command.

section: B. The Verb epaineō — Applaud as Overt Worship
text: The accusative singular direct object is the intensive pronoun autos (αὐτός), used here as a third-person personal pronoun: Him. The final vocative plural is pas (πᾶς) plus laos (λαός), all you peoples — indicating that a large number of people from among the nations cracked the maturity barrier in various periods of history, and prophetically will do so again in the future.

section: C. Dispensational Scope of Psalm 117
text: C. Dispensational Scope of Psalm 117

section: C. Dispensational Scope of Psalm 117
text: Seven principles emerge from the dispensational and eschatological implications of Psalm 117 as cited here.

section: C. Dispensational Scope of Psalm 117
text: First, this entire psalm — two verses — establishes that Gentiles were saved throughout the dispensation of Israel. Gentile believers advanced to spiritual maturity, sometimes with the assistance of Israel and sometimes without it. In every generation of that dispensation, there were saved Gentiles who cracked the maturity barrier.

section: C. Dispensational Scope of Psalm 117
text: Second, the psalm was well-known among the Jewish people, both because of its position at the center of the canon and because, for those positively oriented toward Gentile evangelism, it confirmed the effectiveness of Israel's missionary responsibility. At the same time, its exclusive focus on Gentiles made it unwelcome to those whose orientation was nationalistic rather than doctrinal.

section: C. Dispensational Scope of Psalm 117
text: Third, only a grace-oriented Jewish believer such as Paul could appreciate and cite a psalm that places its entire emphasis on Gentiles. Paul quotes it here because it serves his argument: Christ is the minister to the Gentiles as well as the Jews, and the Old Testament canon itself confirms this.

section: C. Dispensational Scope of Psalm 117
text: Fourth, Psalm 117 describes not merely the historical fact of Gentile salvation but the advance of Gentile believers to spiritual maturity through doctrine resident in the soul. The formula is identical in every dispensation: epignosis doctrine, metabolized through the grace apparatus for perception, is the mechanism of advance.

section: C. Dispensational Scope of Psalm 117
text: Fifth, the psalm is also prophetic and Messianic. It describes the attitude of Gentile believers in the Tribulation — those who, through spiritual maturity, have been preserved in historical catastrophe by the grace of God and who are alive at the second advent of Christ. These Gentile believers form the Gentile cadre for the millennial population.

section: C. Dispensational Scope of Psalm 117
text: Sixth, while the style of the psalm is liturgical — framed by the familiar call to praise — its content is doctrinal. Form and substance serve different functions: the liturgical structure facilitates worship; the doctrinal content sustains it.

section: C. Dispensational Scope of Psalm 117
text: Seventh, the doctrinal implications are both historical and eschatological. Paul quotes the psalm to confirm that Christ is the minister to the Gentiles in every dispensation of history, including those related to unfulfilled prophecy.

section: II. Eschatological Parallels: The Evaluation Events
text: II. Eschatological Parallels: The Evaluation Events

section: II. Eschatological Parallels: The Evaluation Events
text: The worship described prophetically in Psalm 117 is catalogically comparable to the event that follows the resurrection of the Church at the rapture. Prior to the judgment seat of Christ, the resurrected royal family assembles for worship — an event described in Revelation 5 and Revelation 19:1–6. A structurally parallel event occurs at the second advent.

section: II. Eschatological Parallels: The Evaluation Events
text: At the second advent, Old Testament believers — including Gentiles — are resurrected and receive their evaluation, an event comparable in function to the judgment seat of Christ, though distinct from it. Those who cracked the maturity barrier during the age of Israel receive the seventh imputation of blessing to the resurrection body. This evaluation is mentioned by Daniel and confirmed in both Testaments.

section: II. Eschatological Parallels: The Evaluation Events
text: The dispensational structure explains the separate timing. The age of Israel was not terminated but suspended at the ascension of Christ: Christ was resurrected, ascended, and seated at the right hand of the Father without yet possessing a royal family. The Church Age fills that gap. When the Church is completed and removed at the rapture, the age of Israel resumes. The Tribulation terminates it. Then comes the resurrection of Old Testament saints — from Abraham through the Tribulation — followed by their evaluation and, for those who cracked the maturity barrier, the seventh imputation of eternal blessing.

section: II. Eschatological Parallels: The Evaluation Events
text: A third analogous evaluation occurs at the end of the Millennium. Millennial saints are resurrected and evaluated in a comparable event, at which point the seventh imputation of blessing is administered to their resurrection bodies. The Church, Israel, and the Millennium are always kept separate in the plan of God; their respective evaluations are likewise distinct in timing, though identical in function and principle.

section: II. Eschatological Parallels: The Evaluation Events
text: The governing principle is that Gentiles have exactly the same opportunity as Jews. Race, nationality, geographic location, or social status impose no handicap in the plan of God. Doctrine in the soul is the sole operational variable. The Gentile who advances to maturity stands on identical ground with the mature Jewish believer before the justice of God.

section: III. The Fourth Documentation: Isaiah 11:10 (Romans 15:12)
text: III. The Fourth Documentation: Isaiah 11:10 (Romans 15:12)

section: III. The Fourth Documentation: Isaiah 11:10 (Romans 15:12)
text: Paul introduces the fourth and final Old Testament citation with the connective conjunction plus the adverb meaning 'again' — the same formula used for the preceding three citations. The reference is to Isaiah 11:10.

section: A. Introduction of the Citation
text: A. Introduction of the Citation

section: A. Introduction of the Citation
text: Paul's introduction uses the present active indicative of legō (λέγω), meaning to communicate or to say. The present tense is a historical present: it views the past event of Isaiah writing under divine inspiration with the vividness of a present occurrence. Isaiah wrote centuries before Paul, yet the historical present treats his words as if they had been spoken yesterday. The active voice identifies Isaiah as the human author functioning under the ministry of the Holy Spirit, aware that he was writing sacred Scripture. The declarative indicative affirms the absolute reality of Isaiah 11:10 as part of the Old Testament canon.

section: B. The Root Sprout of Jesse
text: B. The Root Sprout of Jesse

section: B. The Root Sprout of Jesse
text: The subject of the quotation is introduced by a predictive future active indicative of eimi (εἰμί), a futuristic use pointing to the first advent of Christ. The declarative indicative mood affirms the absolute and dogmatic reality of that event: the virgin birth, the hypostatic union, the impeccability of Christ from birth through the cross and resurrection, the completed work of reconciliation, propitiation, and redemption, followed by physical death, burial, resurrection, and ascension.

section: B. The Root Sprout of Jesse
text: The predicate nominative is from the noun rhiza (ῥίζα), root. In the Hebrew of Isaiah 11:10 the term is shoresh (שֹׁרֶשׁ), which carries the dual sense of root and sprout. The Greek rhiza functions as an exact equivalent. The proper name Jesse appears in its Hellenized form, Iessai (Ἰεσσαί), indeclinable as a proper name; if declined, it would stand in the ablative of source. The title 'root sprout of Jesse' is Messianic, emphasizing both the Davidic dynasty and the virgin birth. 'Root' points to the source in the lineage of Jesse and David; 'sprout' points to the resurrection — the new life emerging from what was cut down. The generic article comprehends Christ as a single whole in hypostatic union and sets Him apart from all other human beings: He is God in that He differs from humanity; He is man in that He differs from God; He is impeccable in that He differs from the entire human race.

section: C. He Who Shall Rise — Ascensive kai and the Resurrection
text: C. He Who Shall Rise — Ascensive kai and the Resurrection

section: C. He Who Shall Rise — Ascensive kai and the Resurrection
text: The ascensive use of kai (καί) is correctly translated 'even.' It introduces the articular present middle participle of anistēmi (ἀνίστημι), meaning to rise up — both in the sense of coming into historical existence and in the sense of literal bodily resurrection. Both meanings apply to Christ: He came into existence to rule, and He was raised from the dead to rule. Since the title 'root of Jesse' already covers the virgin birth and the existence of the hypostatic union, the participle here points primarily to the resurrection.

section: C. He Who Shall Rise — Ascensive kai and the Resurrection
text: The perfective present tense of the participle denotes the continuation of existing results. Jesus Christ continues in hypostatic union forever. The participle refers to the resurrection as a past event but emphasizes it as a present reality: our Lord is seated at the right hand of the Father in hypostatic union, and the Church is His royal family. The direct middle voice indicates that the subject, the Lord Jesus Christ, participates in the results of His own resurrection. This is a circumstantial participle and constitutes a major element of eschatology.

section: D. To Rule Over Gentiles — the Infinitive archō
text: D. To Rule Over Gentiles — the Infinitive archō

section: D. To Rule Over Gentiles — the Infinitive archō
text: The purpose of the resurrection is stated by the present active infinitive of archō (ἄρχω), to rule. The futuristic present tense denotes an event not yet occurred but regarded as so certain that it is mentally already in existence — the equivalent of the prophetic perfect in Hebrew. The active voice identifies Jesus Christ as the one who produces the action at the second advent and throughout the Millennium. The infinitive expresses actual result.

section: D. To Rule Over Gentiles — the Infinitive archō
text: With the infinitive stands the objective genitive plural of ethnos (ἔθνος), Gentiles. This is precisely why Paul quotes this text: to demonstrate once more from the Old Testament canon itself that Jesus Christ is as much the God of the Gentiles as He is the God of the Jews. In the Millennium, Christ will rule over Old Testament Gentile believers — Nebuchadnezzar, Cyrus the Great, and others who receive their resurrection bodies at the second advent — as well as over surviving Gentile believers of the Tribulation who enter the Millennium to form the cadre of the Gentile millennial population.

section: E. The Guide-On: Christ as the Rallying Standard
text: E. The Guide-On: Christ as the Rallying Standard

section: E. The Guide-On: Christ as the Rallying Standard
text: The Hebrew text of Isaiah 11:10 identifies the root sprout of Jesse as one who 'stands as a guide-on of the peoples.' The guide-on was the military standard of a company or battalion — the rallying point by which scattered troops regrouped after the pressure of combat. Its function was critical: in the chaos following a cavalry charge or infantry engagement, troops oriented on the guide-on to reform their organization and renew their effectiveness. A guide-on that went down meant disorganization, exposure, and destruction.

section: E. The Guide-On: Christ as the Rallying Standard
text: The application is direct. Israel has been scattered through the fifth cycle of discipline — the dispersion. At the second advent, the Lord Jesus Christ stands as the guide-on: the Jews of the dispersion rally to Him for regathering and the fulfillment of the unconditional covenants. But the Gentiles also search for Him. Christ is the rallying point for both. This is confirmed in Revelation 5:5 — 'Behold the lion who is from the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has overcome' — and in Revelation 22:16: 'I, Jesus, am the root and the offspring of David, the bright and morning star.'

section: F. In Him the Gentiles Shall Hope — the Attic Future of elpizō
text: F. In Him the Gentiles Shall Hope — the Attic Future of elpizō

section: F. In Him the Gentiles Shall Hope — the Attic Future of elpizō
text: The final clause of the quotation reads: 'In him shall the Gentiles hope.' The preposition epi (ἐπί) governs the locative case of the intensive pronoun autos (αὐτός) used as a personal pronoun, yielding 'in him.' The subject is the anarthrous plural of ethnos, Gentiles — the absence of the definite article emphasizing quality: these are believing Gentiles, survivors of the Tribulation whose survival is the product of doctrine.

section: F. In Him the Gentiles Shall Hope — the Attic Future of elpizō
text: The verb is the future active indicative of elpizō (ἐλπίζω). Unusually, Paul employs the Attic Greek future form rather than the Koine form. Attic Greek is classical Greek, the language of Athens at its intellectual height. The Koine — common Greek — is the language of the New Testament. Paul's shift from Koine to the Attic future is deliberate and carries honor: he employs the highest register of the Greek language to describe these Gentile believers, whose advance to spiritual maturity under the most extreme historical catastrophe merits distinction. The Attic future is also nomic here — a statement of fact or expected performance. With doctrine to the maximum, the mature believer will hope, will trust, will orient to the Lord Jesus Christ under any condition.

section: F. In Him the Gentiles Shall Hope — the Attic Future of elpizō
text: The active voice identifies the Gentile believer with maximum doctrine resident in the soul as the one producing the action of the verb during the Tribulation. The future tense points to a future event. The declarative indicative is dogmatic: this will happen. Mature Gentile believers will survive the most extreme conditions in human history for one reason — they are absolutely inflexible with regard to the epignosis doctrine in their souls, and totally flexible with regard to the application of that doctrine in the face of historical catastrophe.

section: F. In Him the Gentiles Shall Hope — the Attic Future of elpizō
text: The principle of flexibility requires further definition. Doctrine is the essential; everything else is non-essential. The mature believer is inflexible on doctrine and flexible on non-essentials. This is not compromise or instability — it is the operational expression of strength. Survival through weakness, evasion, or moral capitulation is available to any person; the survival described here is survival through strength, through the honor code, through the functional application of maximum doctrine in the soul to conditions that would destroy a believer without it.

section: IV. The Universal Principle: No Handicap in the Plan of God
text: IV. The Universal Principle: No Handicap in the Plan of God

section: IV. The Universal Principle: No Handicap in the Plan of God
text: The combined testimony of all four Old Testament citations in Romans 15:9–12 establishes a single governing principle: race, nationality, geographic location, social status, and historical circumstance impose no handicap in the plan of God. Gentile believers in the age of the patriarchs, throughout the age of the Law, and prospectively through the Tribulation have always had full access to God's grace and full opportunity for spiritual advance. The operational variable is never external circumstance but internal: the presence or absence of doctrine resident in the soul.

section: IV. The Universal Principle: No Handicap in the Plan of God
text: Paul makes this point through Isaiah's text with particular force. Isaiah 11:10 addresses the second advent directly. It describes the Lord Jesus Christ returning not only to fulfill the unconditional covenants to Israel but to rule over Gentiles and to receive the hope — the confident expectation — of Gentile believers who have advanced to maturity through doctrine. God never welches on an obligation. Every Gentile believer who has followed the plan of God in any dispensation is fully included in the eschatological consummation.

section: IV. The Universal Principle: No Handicap in the Plan of God
text: The dispensational principle is likewise confirmed: the Church and Israel are always kept separate in the plan of God. In the present age, when a Jewish person believes in Christ, that person is no longer identified with Israel dispensationally but becomes part of the Church, the body of Christ, on equal footing with the Gentile believer through the baptism of the Holy Spirit and positional truth. At every stage, the mechanism of blessing is identical: adjustment to the justice of God through faith, followed by the consistent intake of doctrine.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three
text: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 1. Psalm 117 establishes the historical reality of Gentile salvation throughout the dispensation of Israel. Gentile believers existed in every generation, advanced to spiritual maturity through doctrine, and cracked the maturity barrier. The psalm's position at the center of the Hebrew canon gives it canonical weight commensurate with its theological reach.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 2. The imperative of permission governs both verbs of worship in the Psalm 117 citation. The command to praise and to applaud is not imposed against inclination but is in compliance with the mature believer's own desire. Worship at maturity is the natural expression of doctrine resident in the soul — occupation with the person of Christ.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 3. The shift from aineō to epaineō marks a movement from inner praise to overt expression. The prefix epi- adds the sense of applause — an outward, visible manifestation of an inward doctrinal orientation. Mature worship has both an interior dimension (occupation with Christ) and an exterior dimension (overt expression).

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 4. Three structurally parallel evaluation events occur across the dispensations. The judgment seat of Christ follows the rapture for the royal family. A functionally identical event follows the second advent for Old Testament believers, including Gentiles. A third occurs at the end of the Millennium for millennial saints. In each case, those who cracked the maturity barrier receive the seventh imputation of blessing to the resurrection body. The Church, Israel, and the Millennium are always kept distinct.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 5. The title 'root sprout of Jesse' encodes the two advents of Christ. 'Root' points to His origin in the Davidic line through the virgin birth; 'sprout' points to the resurrection — new life emerging from the line that was cut down. The title is Messianic and hypostatic: it emphasizes Christ's humanity as the son of David while presupposing His deity in hypostatic union.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 6. The guide-on metaphor captures the military function of Christ at the second advent. A military guide-on was the standard around which scattered troops rallied after the pressure of engagement. Christ stands as the guide-on for the regathering of Israel and simultaneously for the gathering of Gentile believers who search for Him. Both communities orient on the same rallying point.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 7. Paul's use of the Attic future of elpizō honors the Gentile believers of the Tribulation. The shift from Koine to classical Attic Greek is deliberate — a register elevation that marks these believers as worthy of distinction. The nomic function of the Attic future states a fact of expected performance: with maximum doctrine resident in the soul, the mature believer will orient to Christ under any condition of historical catastrophe.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 8. Survival in historical catastrophe is a function of doctrinal flexibility, not of external advantage. The mature believer is inflexible on doctrine as the essential and flexible on all non-essentials. This is not weakness or compromise but the operational expression of strength through the honor code. It is the same principle operative in every dispensation and is the basis on which Gentile believers will survive the most extreme conditions of the Tribulation.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 9. Race, nationality, and social circumstance impose no handicap in the plan of God. The combined testimony of four Old Testament citations in Romans 15:9–12 establishes this as an absolute principle. The only variable that matters is the presence or absence of doctrine resident in the soul. God never handicaps the believer; the only handicaps that exist are self-imposed through negative volition.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 10. Paul's selection of Moses and Isaiah as his primary Old Testament witnesses reflects a meeting of canonical minds. Moses is the supreme lawgiver-prophet of the Old Testament; Isaiah is its greatest writing prophet. Together, under the ministry of the Holy Spirit, their words provide the doctrinal foundation for Paul's argument that Christ is the minister to both Jews and Gentiles in every dispensation of history.

Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four

section: Romans 15:12–13 — The Royal Family Honor Code: Points 1–6
text: Romans 15:12–13 — The Royal Family Honor Code: Points 1–6

section: Romans 15:12–13 — The Royal Family Honor Code: Points 1–6
text: Romans 15:12–13 “And again Isaiah says, 'The root of Jesse will come, even he who arises to rule the Gentiles; in him will the Gentiles hope.' May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that by the power of the Holy Spirit you may abound in hope.” (ESV)

section: Romans 15:12–13 — The Royal Family Honor Code: Points 1–6
text: Corrected translation: And again Isaiah says, 'The root of Jesse will come, even he who rises to rule the Gentiles; in him will the Gentiles hope.' Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in the sphere of faith, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

section: Romans 15:12–13 — The Royal Family Honor Code: Points 1–6
text: We stand between Romans 15:12 and 15:13. Before verse 13 can be approached, several governing principles must be set in place. The four Old Testament citations that closed the preceding paragraph — documenting that Jesus Christ is the minister to both Jew and Gentile — have established the historical and eschatological framework within which the unique character of the Church Age comes into focus. This chapter develops the Royal Family Honor Code as the operational system of the Christian way of life, the system that makes the Church Age's singular merger of Jew and Gentile under one code both possible and coherent.

section: I. The Uniqueness of the Church Age
text: I. The Uniqueness of the Church Age

section: I. The Uniqueness of the Church Age
text: The four Old Testament citations in the preceding paragraph serve a purpose beyond simple documentation. Taken together they demonstrate that Christ has always been the minister to the Gentiles as well as to the Jews, through every prior dispensation and into the eschatological future of the tribulation and the millennium. But they also illuminate what is absolutely unique about the present dispensation.

section: I. The Uniqueness of the Church Age
text: In every other period of human history, Jew and Gentile operate under different divine codes. Israel functioned under the Mosaic Law — a specialized covenant addressed to one national entity. Gentiles functioned under the laws of divine establishment. In the tribulation and the millennium, this differentiation is restored. But from the Day of Pentecost in AD 30 through the rapture of the Church, there is one and only one period in all of history when Jew and Gentile are merged under a single operational code: the Church Age.

section: I. The Uniqueness of the Church Age
text: The mechanism of this merger is the baptism of the Spirit, retroactive positional truth, and current positional truth. Together these bring every Church Age believer — regardless of ethnic or national origin — into an identical standing in Christ. Christ is not less the minister to either group; He is the prince ruler of the Church, the King of Kings and Lord of Lords, the third category of battlefield royalty. He ministers to both under one code: the Royal Family Honor Code.

section: I. The Uniqueness of the Church Age
text: This uniqueness demands corresponding urgency. The Christian way of life as it actually exists in this dispensation has been buried under layers of historical morality drawn from other dispensations — tithing extracted from the Mosaic Law, ascetic virtue drawn from Gentile establishment norms, various systems of religious self-effort — none of which constitute the Royal Family Honor Code. These are substitutes, and they do not function. The genuine system is what we now examine.

section: II. The Plan of God: X, Y, Z Framework
text: II. The Plan of God: X, Y, Z Framework

section: II. The Plan of God: X, Y, Z Framework
text: The plan of God for the human race can be understood through a three-stage framework designated X, Y, and Z. Each stage is governed by a code, carries its own imputations, and produces its own hope in the technical sense of absolute confidence in a future divine act.

section: Radical X — God's Plan for the Unbeliever
text: Radical X — God's Plan for the Unbeliever

section: Radical X — God's Plan for the Unbeliever
text: Life begins with the divine imputation of human life at physical birth, together with the judicial imputation of Adam's original sin. This is the first judicial imputation: condemnation not on the basis of personal sins but on the basis of Adam's sin. No one is condemned for what he has personally done. Personal sins are already addressed at the cross. Condemnation through Adam always precedes salvation, establishing the first potential: salvation adjustment to the justice of God.

section: Radical X — God's Plan for the Unbeliever
text: The pertinent doctrine is the gospel. Common grace — the Holy Spirit acting on the spiritually dead soul to make the content of the gospel perceivable — produces the first hope: absolute confidence that faith in Christ results in eternal life. When the individual exercises non-meritorious faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, efficacious grace closes the bracket on Radical X with salvation adjustment to the justice of God. The laws of divine establishment sustain the freedom that makes this entire process possible.

section: Radical Y — God's Plan for the Believer in Time
text: Radical Y — God's Plan for the Believer in Time

section: Radical Y — God's Plan for the Believer in Time
text: Radical Y introduces the Royal Family Honor Code as the governing operational system for the believer's advance to spiritual maturity. Two judicial imputations define its structure. The first: all personal sins were imputed to Christ on the cross and judged. The second: at salvation, the righteousness of God is imputed to the believer as the motivating principle of the Christian life. This is God's own righteousness, the undestroyable personal possession of every believer.

section: Radical Y — God's Plan for the Believer in Time
text: These two imputations establish the second potential: the imputation of divine blessing in six categories in time as the sole means of glorifying God during the believer's earthly life. The pertinent doctrine — Bible doctrine perceived through the Grace Apparatus for Perception — produces the second hope: absolute confidence that persistence in doctrine intake will crack the maturity barrier and result in the sixth imputation of blessing. The Royal Family Honor Code is the system that makes this advance possible for the individual without obstructing the advance of every other believer in the same congregation.

section: Radical Z — Glorification
text: Radical Z — Glorification

section: Radical Z — Glorification
text: Radical Z combines the first imputation of Radical X (eternal life at salvation) with the second imputation of Radical Y (blessing in time at maturity) and projects them forward to the third potential: the imputation of great blessing and reward to the resurrection body at the Judgment Seat of Christ. The pertinent doctrine plus undeserved suffering in the advance through Supergrace A, Supergrace B, and Ultra-Supergrace produces the third hope: absolute confidence that at the rapture, in the presence of the Lord in a resurrection body, the seventh imputation of great blessing and reward will be received.

section: Radical Z — Glorification
text: What sustains the experiential function of this entire framework, individually and collectively, throughout the believer's lifetime, is the Royal Family Honor Code. It is not morality. It is not self-sacrifice. It is not any system of religious production. It is the divinely authorized grace system for the royal family of God.

section: III. The Royal Family Honor Code — Points 1–6
text: III. The Royal Family Honor Code — Points 1–6

section: Point 1 — Definition and Description
text: Point 1 — Definition and Description

section: Point 1 — Definition and Description
text: The Royal Family Honor Code is the Christian way of life. It is the system God requires for the individual believer to advance to maturity and simultaneously for all other believers in the same congregation to advance without mutual interference. It prevents one believer from distracting another, from obstructing the issue of Bible doctrine, or from damaging the spiritual momentum of those at a different stage of growth.

section: Point 2 — Aristocracy Always Has Higher Standards
text: Point 2 — Aristocracy Always Has Higher Standards

section: Point 2 — Aristocracy Always Has Higher Standards
text: Every genuine aristocracy is defined by the superiority of its thinking and the standards that thinking produces. Aristocracies emerge because someone at some point possessed superior thinking, and that thinking generated a code. The code gave the group internal coherence, dignity of conduct, and a defined way of resolving conflict. Historical aristocracies have all eventually declined, but they did not begin in decline; they began with standards.

section: Point 2 — Aristocracy Always Has Higher Standards
text: The royal family of God is the one aristocracy that will not decline and cannot be dissolved. Its code is superior to any code any human aristocracy has ever produced, because its source is divine integrity rather than human custom. The progression within this code is: right thinking produces right motivation; right motivation produces right function; right function produces conduct superior to anything achievable by human standards alone.

section: Point 3 — The Doctrinal Basis of Right Thinking
text: Point 3 — The Doctrinal Basis of Right Thinking

section: Point 3 — The Doctrinal Basis of Right Thinking
text: Right thinking and right motivation are based on maximum doctrine resident in the soul, or at minimum whatever doctrine happens to be resident that is pertinent to the situation at hand. There is no substitute for the systematic, sustained intake of Bible doctrine. The believer cannot think rightly about other believers, about circumstances, about God, or about himself without a doctrinal framework in the right lobe of the soul. This is the starting point of all honorable function.

section: Point 4 — The Imputation of Divine Righteousness as the Foundation
text: Point 4 — The Imputation of Divine Righteousness as the Foundation

section: Point 4 — The Imputation of Divine Righteousness as the Foundation
text: At salvation, the justice of God judicially imputes the righteousness of God to every believer. This is a permanent, indestructible possession. It cannot be lost through sin, discipline, reversionism, or any other circumstance. Every believer — regardless of spiritual age, regardless of current behavior — possesses God's perfect righteousness as his or her personal standing before God.

section: Point 4 — The Imputation of Divine Righteousness as the Foundation
text: This is one-half of divine integrity. The justice of God plus the righteousness of God constitutes the holiness of God — the integrity of God. Justice is the function of divine integrity; righteousness is its principle. Every believer possesses the principle. The function of the Royal Family Honor Code is grounded in this fact: because every believer carries imputed divine righteousness, that righteousness commands respect. Possessing God's righteousness is not a static condition; it is a demand for advance in the Christian life.

section: Point 4.5 — The Honor Code as the System of Group Advance
text: Point 4.5 — The Honor Code as the System of Group Advance

section: Point 4.5 — The Honor Code as the System of Group Advance
text: In any local congregation, believers are present at every stage of spiritual growth: the spiritual infant with one percent doctrine and ninety-nine percent human viewpoint; the adolescent believer still dominated by mixed thinking; the mature believer approaching or past the maturity barrier. The question is how this spectrum of spiritual development can coexist in one congregation without the advanced damaging the immature or the immature sabotaging the advanced.

section: Point 4.5 — The Honor Code as the System of Group Advance
text: The answer is the Royal Family Honor Code. God accepts the spiritual infant with his one percent doctrine. The servant is not greater than his master. Therefore the mature believer extends the same acceptance. The infant's errors in human viewpoint are neither attacked nor corrected by confrontation from other believers. The correction comes from doctrine, communicated by the pastor, received by the individual through the Grace Apparatus for Perception. Toleration — not indifference, but principled, deliberate acceptance — is the mechanism that keeps the congregation functional.

section: Point 4.6 — Alignment with the Plan of God
text: Point 4.6 — Alignment with the Plan of God

section: Point 4.6 — Alignment with the Plan of God
text: The Royal Family Honor Code lines up with the plan of God for the believer to advance to maturity, culminating in the sixth imputation of divine blessing. The sixth imputation is the sole means by which God is glorified through the individual believer in time. The Honor Code is therefore not optional supplementary conduct; it is the operational architecture of the divine plan for the Church Age believer.

section: Point 4.7 — Compatibility with the Grace Policy of the Justice of God
text: Point 4.7 — Compatibility with the Grace Policy of the Justice of God

section: Point 4.7 — Compatibility with the Grace Policy of the Justice of God
text: The Honor Code demands that the believer function in full compatibility with the grace policy of the justice of God. All blessing flows from the justice of God, through the grace pipeline, to the righteousness of God. Capacity precedes blessing. God does not impute blessing where there is no capacity to receive it. Doctrine builds capacity; capacity opens the grace pipeline.

section: Point 4.7 — Compatibility with the Grace Policy of the Justice of God
text: Nothing the believer produces — no act of legitimate service, no sacrifice, no giving, no prayer, no witnessing — can break through the encapsulation of the grace pipeline from the outside. Blessing is not earned by production. It is received by the righteousness of God when the justice of God determines that capacity is present. The honor code therefore demands that the believer abandon every attempt to obtain divine blessing through what he does, and rest entirely on the operation of divine integrity.

section: Point 4.8 — The Objective of the Honor Code
text: Point 4.8 — The Objective of the Honor Code

section: Point 4.8 — The Objective of the Honor Code
text: The objective of the Honor Code is advance to spiritual maturity through the daily function of the Grace Apparatus for Perception (GAP), so that the believer operates from the higher ground of resultant integrity. The specific principles of the Honor Code exist to protect and enable this advance. We now turn to those principles.

section: IV. The First Principle: Privacy of the Royal Priesthood
text: IV. The First Principle: Privacy of the Royal Priesthood

section: IV. The First Principle: Privacy of the Royal Priesthood
text: The most foundational principle of the Royal Family Honor Code is the privacy of the royal priesthood. No understanding of the Christian way of life is possible without first understanding that every Church Age believer is a priest.

section: The Structure of Spiritual Freedom
text: The Structure of Spiritual Freedom

section: The Structure of Spiritual Freedom
text: Every believer in the Church Age is a royal priest. A priest represents himself directly before God. There is no mediating human structure between the believer and God in this dispensation. The Levitical priesthood was a specialized, national priesthood for Israel. The family priesthood of the patriarchal age served its dispensational function. But the Church Age is the age of the universal priesthood of the believer. Every believer approaches God directly — not through any human intermediary, not through sacrifice, not through any ecclesiastical structure — directly, in prayer, by name.

section: The Structure of Spiritual Freedom
text: This priesthood carries with it a category of spiritual freedom that runs parallel to the freedom of divine establishment. That freedom requires four defining concepts to be operational:

section: The Structure of Spiritual Freedom
text: First, freedom itself — the liberty to advance or not advance, to accept doctrine or reject it, without coercion from any other believer or any church authority. Second, privacy — freedom is impossible without privacy. Privacy is not limited to what occurs behind closed doors; it includes privacy in public. The manner in which a believer dresses, carries himself, or presents himself in a congregation is his own business. No other believer has the right to intrude upon it. Third, property — freedom cannot exist without the right to property. Property is not merely a civil concept; it is a freedom concept. Any attack on the property of another is an attack on freedom itself. Fourth, the umbrella of authority — freedom does not operate in a vacuum. Authority is the structure within which freedom is protected. In the spiritual realm, this authority flows from God to the Word of God to the delegated authorities of the local church: the pastor-teacher, those with teaching gifts, those with administrative gifts. No believer advances without being under the authority of the Word as communicated through a properly functioning local church.

section: The Practical Implications of Priestly Privacy
text: The Practical Implications of Priestly Privacy

section: The Practical Implications of Priestly Privacy
text: Every believer has the right to assemble in the local church for the purpose of learning doctrine and developing his own norms and standards from the communication of the Word. This right belongs equally to every person present regardless of background, occupation, reputation, or social standing. The congregation of a local church is not a social organization, a counseling service, or a community center. It is a teaching environment. Every intrusion upon a visitor's or member's privacy — demands for personal information, pressure to sign cards, public identification of newcomers, envelopes thrust at new attendees — violates the principle of priestly privacy and constitutes a failure of the Honor Code.

section: The Practical Implications of Priestly Privacy
text: Each believer must approach the Word of God with objectivity. This objectivity is only possible when the believer is confident that whatever passage addresses and convicts him, that conviction comes from the Holy Spirit and not from the exposure of his business to his contemporaries. Once a believer's private life becomes public knowledge within the congregation, objectivity is destroyed. He can no longer hear the Word without filtering it through the awareness of who knows what about him.

section: The Practical Implications of Priestly Privacy
text: Privacy demands that each believer avoid gossip, maligning, judging, implacable criticism, and the mental attitude sins that motivate such activities. It further demands toleration for non-essential opinions within the congregation. Doctrine changes thinking; confrontation does not. The believer who holds wrong opinions will be corrected by doctrine over time if the congregation protects his freedom to hear it.

section: V. The Second Principle: Impersonal Love
text: V. The Second Principle: Impersonal Love

section: V. The Second Principle: Impersonal Love
text: The second tenet of the Royal Family Honor Code is impersonal love. This command cannot be properly understood until the distinction between personal and impersonal love is clear.

section: Personal Love — Limited and Object-Centered
text: Personal Love — Limited and Object-Centered

section: Personal Love — Limited and Object-Centered
text: Personal love emphasizes the object. It is by definition limited to a small number of people. Category one personal love has as its object the Lord Jesus Christ, the revealed member of the Godhead; this level of love comes only from maximum doctrine in the soul. Category two is the right man or right woman in the divinely designed relationship of marriage — strictly limited to one person of the opposite sex. Category three encompasses friends and family — still a comparatively small circle.

section: Personal Love — Limited and Object-Centered
text: Personal love is not commanded as the organizing principle of Christian conduct toward the congregation. It is a result of spiritual advance, not a means of it, and it cannot serve as the standard for how believers treat one another in general. Requiring personal affection toward every believer in the congregation would be both psychologically impossible and theologically incorrect.

section: Impersonal Love — Unlimited and Subject-Centered
text: Impersonal Love — Unlimited and Subject-Centered

section: Impersonal Love — Unlimited and Subject-Centered
text: Impersonal love emphasizes the subject. It is unlimited in its scope. Its object is every believer — the spiritual infant, the adolescent, the mature believer, and the reversionist. It is called impersonal because it does not depend on the attractiveness, behavior, attitude, or reciprocation of the object. It is entirely governed by the doctrinal norms and standards resident in the soul of the subject.

section: Impersonal Love — Unlimited and Subject-Centered
text: The command love the brethren is a command to impersonal love. It is what was formerly described as a relaxed mental attitude — a term abandoned in favor of impersonal love because the earlier phrase failed to communicate that it is a category of love with a specific object and a specific standard. The standard is your own integrity, not the other person's conduct.

section: Impersonal Love — Unlimited and Subject-Centered
text: Impersonal love as the command to love one's neighbor as oneself does not mean that the intensity of feeling directed toward oneself is to be redirected toward the neighbor. It means that the norms and standards by which you govern your own conduct are the basis on which you treat those in your periphery. You do not like or dislike on the basis of their behavior. You treat them on the basis of your integrity.

section: The Operational Content of Impersonal Love
text: The Operational Content of Impersonal Love

section: The Operational Content of Impersonal Love
text: Impersonal love, when properly functional, excludes retaliation, revenge, counter-attack, counter-gossip, and all forms of personality conflict. When a fellow believer maligns, gossips, judges, or attacks, the response of impersonal love is silence on the matter and stability in one's own conduct. To retaliate is to descend to the standard of the attacker. The moment the attacked party retaliates, the issue shifts from a contrast between integrity and failure to a mutually destructive exchange in which neither party can be evaluated by an external standard.

section: The Operational Content of Impersonal Love
text: Impersonal love excludes carrying a grudge. Every believer, including the most obnoxious one in the congregation, carries the imputation of divine righteousness. To hold a grudge against another believer is to bear a grudge against the righteousness of God resident in that believer. That is both presumptuous and theologically untenable.

section: The Operational Content of Impersonal Love
text: Impersonal love is not manufactured by effort. It is the product of the filling of the Holy Spirit and the application of doctrine to experience. It is the practical expression of the believer's own doctrinal norms and standards in relationship to others. It cannot be reduced to the level of reciprocal response — treating people well because they treat you well. It must function regardless of how the object behaves.

section: VI. Point 4 — The Common Objective
text: VI. Point 4 — The Common Objective

section: VI. Point 4 — The Common Objective
text: The Royal Family Honor Code recognizes a single common objective for every believer in time: advance to maturity adjustment to the justice of God through maximum doctrine resident in the soul, sustained by perseverance in the perception of doctrine.

section: VI. Point 4 — The Common Objective
text: This objective can only be attained through systematic Bible teaching. The believer must identify his own right pastor and remain under that ministry — not as a constraint on intellectual freedom, but as the only way to receive structured, systematic theology that builds the doctrinal framework necessary for genuine advance. Theological tourism — moving from one speaker to the next in search of novelty — produces only fragmentary knowledge. Systematic theology requires sustained exposure to one coherent doctrinal system over time.

section: VI. Point 4 — The Common Objective
text: The pastor's authority extends to teaching doctrine and enforcing policy in the local church. It does not extend to functioning as a referee in personal disputes or marital conflicts. His task is to ensure the freedom, privacy, and functional honor code love of the congregation — the conditions under which the common objective can be pursued.

section: VI. Point 4 — The Common Objective
text: Freedom plus equal opportunity produces inequality. Under the Royal Family Honor Code, every believer has equal opportunity to advance through his priestly function and the reception of doctrine. What each believer does with that opportunity — positive volition producing advance, negative volition producing reversionism, or some oscillation between the two — creates legitimate inequalities. These inequalities are the direct product of freedom. They are not to be corrected by coercion but respected as the expression of each believer's own volitional choices before God.

section: VI. Point 4 — The Common Objective
text: These temporal inequalities are carried forward into eternity. At the Judgment Seat of Christ, some will receive great blessing and reward imputed to the resurrection body; some will receive the resurrection body without such reward. This is not a cause for regret in eternity — Scripture is clear that sorrow, tears, and pain are removed at death. But it is a reason for urgency in time. The motivation for advance must arise from the believer's own inner resources, from the doctrinal norms and standards established in the right lobe of the soul.

section: VII. Point 5 — Integrity Includes But Exceeds Morality
text: VII. Point 5 — Integrity Includes But Exceeds Morality

section: VII. Point 5 — Integrity Includes But Exceeds Morality
text: The Royal Family Honor Code builds integrity but does not reject morality. These are not synonyms, and the distinction is critical.

section: VII. Point 5 — Integrity Includes But Exceeds Morality
text: Morality is the standard designed for the fulfillment of the laws of divine establishment. It is addressed to the entire human race — believer and unbeliever alike. It is the product of divine establishment operating through human society to sustain the conditions under which freedom can exist and the plan of God can advance. Morality is legitimate, necessary, and not to be dismissed.

section: VII. Point 5 — Integrity Includes But Exceeds Morality
text: But morality is not the Christian way of life. The error of identifying Christianity with morality is the error of confusing an establishment norm designed for all mankind with a grace system designed specifically for the royal family of God in the Church Age. The Honor Code does not exclude morality; it exceeds morality. It demands a higher standard rooted not in social convention or legal code but in the integrity of God as reflected through the imputed righteousness of God in the soul of the believer.

section: VII. Point 5 — Integrity Includes But Exceeds Morality
text: This higher standard has its source in two things: the filling of the Holy Spirit, and Bible doctrine previously learned and resident in the soul. Integrity produced by this combination operates above the level of morality — it includes moral conduct but it is not reducible to it. The Christian way of life is above morality; it encompasses morality within a larger and superior framework of divine integrity operating through the grace pipeline.

section: VIII. Point 6 — The Honor Code Excludes Production as the Means of Blessing
text: VIII. Point 6 — The Honor Code Excludes Production as the Means of Blessing

section: VIII. Point 6 — The Honor Code Excludes Production as the Means of Blessing
text: The Royal Family Honor Code excludes all forms of Christian production, works, talent, and self-sacrifice as the means of receiving divine blessing. This is among the most frequently misunderstood principles in the Christian life.

section: VIII. Point 6 — The Honor Code Excludes Production as the Means of Blessing
text: Nothing the believer does — whether it is legitimate production commanded by Scripture or self-generated religious effort — can elicit blessing from the justice of God. Not witnessing. Not giving. Not prayer as a substitute for doctrine. Not sacrificial service. Not asceticism. Not personality change. Not moral reformation. None of these, individually or combined, can break through the encapsulation of the grace pipeline from the production side. The justice of God is not moved by what the believer does.

section: VIII. Point 6 — The Honor Code Excludes Production as the Means of Blessing
text: The justice of God imputes blessing to the righteousness of God in the believer when capacity exists. Capacity is built exclusively by the intake of Bible doctrine through the Grace Apparatus for Perception. The attainment of maturity through maximum doctrine resident in the soul is the only means of divine blessing in the primary sense — with one exception: blessing by association with a mature believer, whereby those in the periphery of a supergrace believer receive logistical grace overflow.

section: VIII. Point 6 — The Honor Code Excludes Production as the Means of Blessing
text: The distinction between the royal priesthood and the royal ambassadorship clarifies the role of production. Every believer is both a priest and an ambassador. The priesthood is the sphere of advance — the daily function of the Grace Apparatus for Perception builds doctrine in the soul, cracks the maturity barrier, and produces capacity. The ambassadorship is the sphere of production — what the believer does as a result of maturity. Production is always the result of advance, never the means of it.

section: VIII. Point 6 — The Honor Code Excludes Production as the Means of Blessing
text: Between the cross and the maturity barrier, every believer is sustained by logistical grace: the provision of everything necessary for physical existence and spiritual advance — food, shelter, transportation, the right pastor, the right circumstances. This is not yet the blessing of the sixth imputation; it is the grace provision that keeps the believer alive and in a position to advance. The sixth imputation — the great blessing imputed at maturity — is the goal. It is integrity to integrity: the integrity of God reaching down the grace pipeline to the imputed righteousness of God in the mature believer.

section: VIII. Point 6 — The Honor Code Excludes Production as the Means of Blessing
text: The Honor Code demands total dependence on the integrity of God. God recognizes integrity. He does not recognize effort, sincerity, sacrifice, or religious production as the basis for blessing. He recognizes His own righteousness imputed to the believer and blesses on that basis when the believer has developed the capacity to receive it. This is the grace system. This is the Christian way of life.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 1. The Church Age is dispensationally unique: it is the only period in human history when Jew and Gentile operate under a single divine code. The four Old Testament citations in Romans 15 document Christ as the minister to both groups across all dispensations, and in doing so they illuminate the singular character of the present age.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 2. The X–Y–Z framework governs the plan of God for every human being: Radical X covers the unbeliever and salvation adjustment; Radical Y covers the believer's advance to maturity through the Royal Family Honor Code; Radical Z covers glorification at the Judgment Seat of Christ. Each stage has its own imputations, its own pertinent doctrine, and its own absolute hope.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 3. The Royal Family Honor Code is the Christian way of life in the Church Age: it is not morality, not religious production, not self-sacrifice, and not any form of legalism. It is the grace-based operational system by which the royal family of God advances collectively without mutual interference.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 4. The privacy of the royal priesthood is the most foundational principle of the Honor Code: every believer is his own priest before God, approaching God directly and without human mediation. This priesthood carries with it freedom, privacy, the right to property, and submission to the umbrella of spiritual authority. All four are necessary; none can be removed without destroying the others.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 5. Impersonal love is the operating command of the Honor Code toward fellow believers: it emphasizes the doctrinal norms and standards of the subject rather than the behavior, attractiveness, or reciprocation of the object. It excludes retaliation, revenge, gossip, grudges, and personality conflict. It is the product of the filling of the Holy Spirit and resident doctrine — not of effort or emotional resolve.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 6. Freedom plus equal opportunity produces inequality: under the Honor Code every believer has equal opportunity to advance, but volitional choices produce legitimate inequalities in spiritual growth. These inequalities are transferred into eternity as differential reward at the Judgment Seat of Christ. They are not to be coercively equalized; they are to be respected as the expression of each believer's freedom.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 7. Integrity includes but exceeds morality: morality is a standard for the entire human race under the laws of divine establishment. The Honor Code does not reject morality but surpasses it, demanding a higher standard rooted in the integrity of God operating through imputed righteousness and the filling of the Holy Spirit.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 8. Production is always the result of advance, never its means: the justice of God blesses through the grace pipeline to the righteousness of God when capacity exists. No act of legitimate production, sacrifice, or religious effort can substitute for capacity built by the intake of Bible doctrine. The believer's advance to maturity is entirely a priesthood function — the Grace Apparatus for Perception — not an ambassadorship function.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 9. The common objective of the Honor Code demands systematic theology under one ministry: theological mobility — moving from teacher to teacher in search of novelty — produces only fragmentary knowledge. The believer must identify his right pastor-teacher and remain under that ministry to receive the structured, cumulative doctrinal framework necessary for genuine advance to maturity.

section: Glossary for Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: The first and most foundational principle of the Royal Family Honor Code. Every Church Age believer is a royal priest who approaches God directly without human mediation. This priesthood carries four necessary components: freedom, privacy, the right to property, and submission to the umbrella of spiritual authority. The invasion of any believer's privacy by another believer is a violation of this principle.

section: Glossary for Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four

section: Glossary for Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: The Spirit-enabled process by which Bible doctrine is received, processed, and internalized in the right lobe of the soul as epignosis — full, exact knowledge. The daily function of GAP is the sole means of building capacity for divine blessing and advancing toward the maturity barrier.

text: God's provision of everything necessary for the believer's physical existence and continued opportunity for spiritual advance between salvation and the maturity barrier: food, shelter, transportation, the right pastor, the right circumstances. Distinct from the sixth imputation of blessing at maturity; logistical grace sustains the believer in a position to advance regardless of his current stage of growth.

section: Glossary for Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four

section: Glossary for Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: The third category of adjustment to the justice of God. Progressive; achieved through the daily intake of Bible doctrine over time, culminating in the cracking of the maturity barrier and the sixth imputation of divine blessing in time. Distinct from salvation adjustment (instantaneous, once) and rebound adjustment (instantaneous, repeated as needed).

section: Glossary for Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four

section: Glossary for Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: Stages of spiritual maturity beyond the maturity barrier. Supergrace A designates the initial cracking of the maturity barrier with reception of the sixth imputation of blessing. Supergrace B and Ultra-supergrace designate continued advance in doctrine and capacity beyond that threshold, with increasing reception of divine blessing and increasing capacity to glorify God in time.

section: Glossary for Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four

section: Glossary for Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: An imputation made by the justice of God on a legal rather than a residential basis. The seven judicial imputations in the plan of God include: Adam's sin to the human race at birth; all personal sins to Christ on the cross; divine righteousness to the believer at salvation; and great blessing and reward to the resurrection body at the Judgment Seat of Christ.

section: Glossary for Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: Umbrella of authority

section: Glossary for Chapter Four Hundred Eighty-Four
text: The hierarchical structure of delegated spiritual authority within which the believer's freedom operates. Flows from God, to the Word of God, to the pastor-teacher and other gifted communicators, to the administrative structure of the local church. No believer advances spiritually outside of submission to this structure.
